event.active_blue_east_blue_01_baratie_s: {{npc_rohan}} wipes his hands, checks your crew capacity, and accepts a berth aboard.
You pay for the dishes prepared for the passing crew.
{{npc_rohan}} trades schedules, cargo talk, and customer rumors without promising to leave.
At Baratie, {{npc_rohan}} finishes a service for a crew that has just left him without a berth. His knives are packed; his bag is already tied.
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_beach_wre: You refuse to decide who owns what the sea threw back.
You assign the wreck to the wrong flag and trigger an expensive dispute.
You also identify the last repair, recent enough to trace the owner.
The marks remain ambiguous and nobody yields the cargo.
You find the yard mark and hull number beneath the weed.
Both groups accuse you of favoring the other and keep everything.
The split is clean enough that both sides pay you.
You get a truce but no clear split.
The fishers and merchant accept a written split.
A small wreck has washed onto an East Blue beach. Fishers are already pulling planks free while a merchant claims to recognize the cargo.
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_clinic_tr: A merchant captain sells medical stores at a steep price.
Buy from a ship
{{npc_ari}} agrees to come aboard after finishing the shift.
Offer {{npc_ari}} a berth
Sheets become bandages clean enough to last the night.
Sacrifice clean cloth
Calm returns, but {{npc_ari}} is holding the last clean roll. Two patients are still bleeding, and port supplies will not arrive before dawn.
The Last Bandage
An argument breaks out and overturns a treatment tray.
The whole room follows your directions until help arrives.
The crowd quiets a little but keeps crowding {{npc_ari}}.
Families step back and finally leave a lane for emergencies.
Calm the room
You empty the clean-linen cabinets and bring supplies to the treatment tables.
Fetch supplies
You prioritize badly and a minor injury takes the last useful dose.
You even establish a clean flow to prevent cross-infection.
You stabilize the line, but too slowly to prevent shortages.
You separate emergencies, fractures, and simple wounds before {{npc_ari}} runs out of hands.
Triage the injured
A dock collision floods the local clinic at once. {{npc_ari}} no longer has enough hands to sort injuries, panicked families, and vanishing supplies.
The Clinic Overflows
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_coastal_t: You leave the fake toll behind.
Bin the notice
Port authorities refund part of what you paid.
Claim your payment back
Your account completes the amounts and descriptions of the gang.
Send your account
Three months later, a notice circulates through East Blue ports: the fake toll has been broken up. Victims are now comparing their receipts.
The Impossible Receipt
You keep the clipping as proof that a small racket can leave a lasting trail.
Keep the clipping
You let the story close with the newspaper.
Move on
Three months after the notice, a short gazette confirms the racketeers were convicted. The copied receipts were enough to link their boats.
The False Toll Falls
The men laugh and double the fee while pointing weapons.
Two rowers realize they have no official cover and stop following.
They lower the price a little but keep the racket.
Their leader backs down when you ask which office signed their order.
Call their bluff
You cut too close to a shoal and scrape the hull before escaping.
You even pin them in your lee before breaking away.
You outrun them, but only after straining the rig.
You take a wind they cannot hold and leave them behind.
Outmaneuver them
You pay their “toll” and continue without a fight.
Pay the toll
An armed skiff cuts across your path and demands a toll “for the coast.” It carries neither kingdom flag nor Marine insignia.
The Flagless Toll
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_coastwatc: You compare cargoes and ringing times, then ask to be written if the pattern returns.
Follow the ledgers
You help restore the station and promise to answer their news.
Join the watch
You refuse to pick a side but leave a way to reach you.
Leave a contact
Under the bell, the clapper bears two marks: an old crack and a fresh cut. The keepers split between repairing the station and investigating false signals.
The Split Clapper
Several ports receive the times and cargo marks.
Circulate the pattern
The keepers keep recording without warning the broker.
Keep it quiet
Merchants pay to receive suspicious timings before departure.
Sell the warning to merchants
A year later, the ledgers arrive by courier. The false rings now follow the same three cargoes, all insured by the same broker.
The First Year’s Books
The money pays for rope, oil, and fittings for the season.
Send Berrys
Your notes reach both neighboring posts with repair plans.
Share their method
The keepers begin coordinating watches instead of maintaining three full teams.
Propose a shared watch
A year later, a letter from the keepers finds you: the bell works, but two neighboring posts have gone silent for lack of money and hands.
The First Season
You propose that major merchants fund upkeep in exchange for detailed reports.
Fund it by subscription
You ask the three stations to remain a simple coastal chain instead of growing too fast.
Keep it local
You urge the stations to share schedules, failures, and warnings freely with every port.
Open the network
Thirty months after your first visit, a letter recounts the storm: three stations rang together and an entire convoy changed course in time. The keepers ask how the network should develop.
The Three-Bell Storm
Several ports contribute a small fixed share to upkeep.
Accept port dues
You back a public collection and the network stays open to everyone.
Keep it free
The keepers keep your contact but now make decisions without you.
Step back
Two years later, a gazette prints the free network schedule. Fishers use it as much as large cargo ships, but donations barely cover repairs.
The Open Bells
You back keepers who now send the same warning to every ship.
Equalize the alerts
Companies keep priority and fund rapid expansion.
Honor the contracts
Danger warnings become public; only commercial reports stay paid.
Split the service
Two years later, subscriptions have paid for new bells. But small boats complain they receive warnings after the companies funding the network.
The Contract Bells
Each station keeps its own rules but shares emergency signals with the others.
Let each coast decide
The network writes public safety ahead of every commercial contract.
Safety before profit
The network reserves enough income to depend on no kingdom or company.
A self-funded watch
Years after the first bell, three veteran keepers write together. Their chain now covers several East Blue coasts and needs one common principle before expanding further.
The Keepers Return
The keepers send you a share from their recognition fund.
Accept their stipend
You refuse signature and money: the chain now belongs to those who ring it.
Leave the legacy to them
Your name joins those who shaped East Blue’s watch chain.
Sign their charter
Nearly ten years after your first visit, a letter bears the mark of several coastal stations. The old bell still exists, but it is no longer alone.
The Bell You Hear Everywhere
You put down enough money to restore the bell before the next night.
Fund a repair
The bracket breaks under your test and the bell drops into the sand.
You also identify why the corrosion returns every season.
You find the crack too late to stop the clapper failing.
You spot a worn pin nobody could see from the beach.
Inspect the bell
You mix up two different nights and accuse an innocent fisher.
You even link the false rings to an old coastal smuggling route.
You confirm the false signals without finding who causes them.
The times reveal someone rings just before certain cargo ships pass.
Compare the reports
On an East Blue coast, an old warning bell sometimes rings with no ship in danger—then stays silent when real fog comes in.
The Coastwatch Bell
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_cocoyasi_: Planks and chain hold the gate until repairs.
Brace it with scrap
A carpenter replaces the hinge before the next tide.
Pay a carpenter
Families move tools and harvests before the next tide.
Warn the lower fields
Water returns, but a small side gate remains open toward the lower fields. If it breaks, the next tide will flood them again.
The Second Gate
You help farmers save the nearest plants without fixing the canal.
Carry water by hand
The gate gives at once and the timber slams your side.
You also brace the split beam before it can fall again.
You free it halfway; water runs, but tears out a bank.
The gate rises and fresh water returns to the canal.
Lift the gate
You open the wrong ditch and salt water pushes in faster.
You also work out why the tide blocks the canal every week.
You find the blockage, but only after losing part of the flow.
You find a flap jammed beneath weeds and clear it.
Trace the blockage
In Cocoyasi Village, irrigation stops as the tide rises. The first ditches already taste of salt, and farmers run toward the gate.
The Salted Channel
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_contraban: The vials sink. The skiff immediately vanishes behind the swell.
Dump the vials
You keep the abbreviations in mind and throw the vials overboard.
Memorize the list
You signal for them to take the bundle back. They refuse and pull away.
Signal the skiff
The bundle holds unmarked vials and a list of abbreviated ports. A dark skiff stays just close enough to watch what you do.
The Bundle Opened
You send enough Berrys to close the debt without endorsing their trade.
Pay them off
Your silence becomes an answer; they promise to remember your name.
Send nothing
You send back the copied abbreviations with one line: “Change your route.”
Send their list back
Six months later, a note slipped under a door bears the same tarred knot: “You owe us a bundle, or an explanation.”
The Black Knot
The trade stops being your concern.
Forget them
You keep the knot pattern in mind for future docks.
Keep watching
You let the small war end without hunting the last smugglers.
Take the win
A year after the bundle, an East Blue gazette reports several smuggling skiffs have left those same ports. The black knot stops appearing.
A Route Abandoned
The blade slips and the swell slams you against the hull.
You also recover the marked knot that identifies the gang.
You cut one line, but the bundle remains caught under the rudder.
The bundle comes free before it can damage the rudder.
Cut it free
You leave the bundle alone while it does not threaten the rudder.
Hold course
You follow a false trace and hit floating debris.
You also catch its hooded lamp behind a swell.
The wake fades before you can link the bundle to a boat.
You pick out the small wake of a boat that just left your stern.
Find their wake
A dull thump hits beneath your ship. A tarred bundle is tied to the rudder, planted overnight without anyone boarding.
Below the Waterline
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_crew_noti: {{npc_owen}} inspects your hull for a day’s wage and leaves you a repair list.
You note departures, full crews, and the berths still open.
{{npc_owen}} hears your offer, checks the available berth, and accepts a place aboard.
In an East Blue port, {{npc_owen}} removes his notice from the crew board: his previous captain sailed without paying for repairs.
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_dockyard_: You spread their story among other ports.
Spread the case
You leave them the evidence and step out of the dispute.
Leave them the copy
Your receipt completes their wage case.
Send your receipt
Five months later, a workers’ letter finds you: the copied ledger forced the yard to reopen its accounts. One week of wages is still missing.
The Copied Names
Your name remains tied to the case in the yard.
Accept their thanks
For you too, the account is finally closed.
Close the book
The worker returns what you fronted.
Take back your advance
Ten months after the first ledger, the workers report that the yard paid the balance and now posts hours before each payday.
The Closed Account
You copy the crossed-out names before the foreman closes the ledger.
Copy the missing names
You front one worker’s wage and keep the receipt.
Pay one worker
You refuse to sign a ledger you did not keep.
Refuse the dispute
In an East Blue shipyard, six workers wait for wages. The foreman shows a ledger where their names were crossed out the night before.
The Wage Book
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_fish_mark: You demand a share of the repayments in exchange for your testimony.
Demand a cut
You refuse to prolong the matter. The thread ends for you.
Drop the matter
Your account joins the case built by cheated merchants.
Send your testimony
Four months later, an East Blue letter arrives: the rigged scale has moved from market to market, and several sellers are now blaming one another.
The Same Scale
The settlement includes a small payment for witnesses who helped establish the fraud.
Accept the witness payment
The news leaves with the paper.
Move on
You keep proof that one small rule changed.
Keep the clipping
An East Blue gazette finally reports the settlement: merchants caught with false weights repay customers, and markets now display reference weights.
The Stalls’ Judgment
The vendor pockets your money and promises to fix the weights—a weak promise.
Buy the vendor’s silence
Customers compare baskets. The vendor folds his awning under jeers.
Call out the stall
You discreetly mark the true weight under the tray, leaving proof for later customers.
Mark the scale
At the fish market, an old customer taps two identical weights: one rings hollow. The vendor is already trying to pack away his scale.
Hollow Weights
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_fishing_n: Your shipwright braces the winch; the fisher gets free without sacrificing the whole net.
Brace the winch
The tension drops and the fisher stays aboard, but a morning catch escapes.
Cut the net
Several hands pull the fisher free of the line before the winch starts again.
Haul him back
The net survives the crossing, then its winch jams. A fisher is caught by the ankle and slides toward the rail while the shoal pulls the other end.
The Winch Jams
You mistake a submerged float for a gap and pull the net against the bow.
You also spot the winch straining abnormally on the leeward fishing boat.
You avoid the main net, but a side line wraps beneath the hull.
The floats reveal the net pocket before it closes your passage.
Read the floats
You kill your speed and let the fishers open a lane.
Slow down and hail
The keel catches the lead line; the net whips the rudder before tearing free.
You cross without touching a mesh and even signal the current to the fishers.
You clear the net, but floats hammer the hull and tear one line loose.
You read the net drift and pass through its only opening.
Thread the gap
At dawn, two East Blue fishing boats close a channel with a huge, nearly invisible net. Your bow is coming fast as the floats vanish under a short swell.
The Net Across the Channel
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_fog_bell_: The skiff is free, but the marker will stay silent until repaired.
Cut the chain
You keep distance and guide a towboat to him once the fog lifts.
Mark his position
You pull the skiff free of the chain and the bell starts ringing again.
Tow him clear
Near the marker, a keeper struggles in a small skiff: the bell chain has fouled beneath his keel.
The Marker Skiff
You anchor clear of the breakers and wait for the fog to open a path.
Anchor until clear
You mistake an echo and advance toward rock.
You also hear a small metal hammer near the marker.
You avoid the first rock, but the second scrapes the planking.
The rhythm of breakers sketches the coast through the fog.
Listen for breakers
The bottom rises faster than expected and the keel touches.
You find both the channel and the exact position of the silent marker.
You find the channel, but only after scraping a shoal.
The soundings trace a safe channel despite the silent bell.
Sound the depth
Fog swallows the East Blue coast and the reef bell stays silent. Each wave throws a different echo off unseen rocks.
The Silent Fog Bell
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_goa_gate_: Nobody passes until the guards drop the surcharge.
Block the gate
The chain rises and the cart passes before the fee changes again.
Cover their passage
You leave the gate with the duplicate ledger numbers in mind.
Leave with the proof
A servants’ cart remains blocked despite the commotion. Guards demand one more fee before lifting the chain.
The Servants’ Cart
The crowd turns on you when guards threaten to close the gate.
Even a palace officer demands the ledger after hearing the crowd.
Counting resumes, but the poorest carts remain blocked.
The clerk recounts in public and several surcharges vanish.
Demand a public count
You pay only your own line and pass the gate.
Pay your line
You search the wrong cart and the guards charge you for the delay.
You find the column reserving exemptions for wealthy crests.
You see the discrepancies, but the clerk closes the book before you can prove them.
You spot the same goods charged twice under different names.
Find the duplicate ledger
At a gate in Goa Kingdom, modest carts pay twice while crested carriages pass through. A clerk hides a second ledger beneath the desk.
The Gate Ledger
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_harbor_qu: You learn he paid a sailor to leave an island without telling his family.
Hear his story
You buy him a meal before the adults decide what happens next.
Buy him a meal
Port authorities register him before investigating who brought him aboard.
Turn him over to the port
During the examination, a teenager emerges from a side hold. He is not sick, but nobody listed him on the ship’s manifest.
The Hidden Passenger
The cordon breaks and the crowd floods the gangway.
Dockworkers and families organize their own line away from the gangway.
You keep the crowd out, but rumors are already spreading through the port.
You win enough calm for the clinic to examine the crew.
Hold the cordon
You misread the signs and needlessly expose several dockers.
You even trace the cause to a badly stored fish barrel.
You rule out the worst, but too late to prevent panic.
You recognize food poisoning, not a contagious fever.
Inspect the symptoms
You stay behind the rope until the official diagnosis.
Respect quarantine
A merchant ship docks under a yellow flag. Three sailors are vomiting on deck while families and dockworkers already crowd the cordon.
The Yellow Flag
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_loguetown: The yard releases a dinghy and records the sale.
The yard prepares a sloop for your departure.
You leave with prices, visible flaws, and no debt.
In Loguetown, a shipyard displays several hulls ready to sail. The foreman knocks on each plank and calls out prices to buyers.
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_marine_ch: You refuse to become the owner’s guarantor.
Let the owner answer
You quote the posted fee in front of the soldiers. Several eyes leave the deputy.
Name the false fee
You pay to move the line and remember the deputy’s face.
Pay to clear the line
A crate opens: nothing illegal, only food already taxed. The deputy still holds out his hand to the owner.
The Open Crate
The officer cuts you off and seizes a crate as an “inspection fee.”
Dockworkers repeat your figures loudly enough to draw the post commander.
You get a regular inspection, but only after a made-up fine.
The soldiers return to the official manifest and stop the extractions.
Press the manifest
You accuse the wrong man and the inspection turns hostile.
You also spot the second ledger hidden under the table.
You see the tension, but not its source before the crates are opened.
You spot the deputy diverting every crate before it reaches the ledger.
Read the officer
You let the crates be opened one by one without provoking the post.
Submit to the search
At an East Blue coastal post, Marines hold a line of cargo. A deputy demands “inspection fees” absent from the official manifest.
The Crate Inspection
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_marine_pa: You help the clerk close cleanly and send the crowd to the next service.
You front enough to feed one recruit and keep the receipt for tomorrow.
You sort the sheets by unit; the missing pay records surface before closing.
At an East Blue Marine office, the pay shutter comes down with a dozen sailors still waiting. The clerk says one ledger is missing and refuses to reopen the cashbox.
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_market_br: You keep onlookers from pocketing the fallen rolls until the merchant returns.
You keep a small payment for securing the safe.
You leave guards and merchants to handle their money.
A cart snaps an axle in the market. A small safe springs open on impact, and rolls of Berrys scatter between boots.
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_merchant_: You keep contact with the convoy.
Answer the merchants
You offer to escort them again when routes cross.
Ask for work
You thank them and leave the convoy to its routes.
Close the correspondence
Nine months later, a convoy letter finds you: the delayed captain survived, and the merchants remember the slot you held—or refused.
Nine Months After the Squall
You send the money back to the ship that took the worst damage.
Send it back
The payment arrives with the accounts.
Take the share
You refuse the share but leave your name in their ledger of reliable captains.
Refuse money, keep the name
A second letter arrives with the yearly accounts: the convoy opened a steadier route and pays those who helped during its worst crossing.
The Convoy Share
You refuse to join a formation you do not know.
Keep your own route
You pass your heading to the lost ship without joining formation.
Share your heading
You close the convoy gap until the delayed ship returns.
Take the empty slot
An East Blue merchant convoy crosses your course with an empty slot in the middle. The missing ship flashes far behind, separated by a squall.
The Convoy Gap
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_mirrorbal: You hold the batten until everyone clears the stage.
Hold the batten
You leave the technicians to recover their stage.
Leave backstage
The performers bow in front of the fallen curtain as if it were planned.
Make it the finale
The mechanism moves again, then a second rope snaps: the curtain drops behind the performers instead of in front of them.
The Curtain Drops
The batten spins and throws you into the scenery.
You realign the whole rig without stopping the music.
You stop the curtain, but tear the main backdrop.
You free the pulley before the performers enter.
Climb the rig
The curtain drops cleanly to the floor; the show continues without scenery.
Cut the curtain
Your diversion turns into a commotion and seats break.
The crowd even calls for your name before the performers return.
The crowd grumbles until the stage resumes.
You turn the wait into a game and keep the room with you.
Hold the crowd
On Mirrorball Island, the main curtain jams above a full stage. The metal batten shudders while the audience is already stamping its feet.
The Jammed Curtain
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_night_anc: The anchor bites again and the ship stops drifting.
You choose to drift offshore rather than risk a broken chain.
Everyone takes a station until the bottom is safe again.
At night anchorage, the coast slowly grows closer instead of staying fixed. The anchor is dragging while the wind turns toward the rocks.
event.active_blue_east_blue_01_night_wat: You force the saboteurs to dump their lantern before fleeing.
Chase the boat
The decoy sinks with its lenses.
Destroy the false light
You keep course and pass the position to the next port.
Mark the position
Along the reef, you spot a small boat beneath the false lantern. Someone is already folding the signal light to disappear.
One Light Too Many
You stop advancing until the coast can be read.
Heave to
You mistake a reflection for the main signal and guide the ship toward shoals.
You even read the deliberate offset between the lamps and spot the trap.
You read the code too late; the hull scrapes a tongue of rock.
You separate the true light from the decoy and correct course.
Read the light pattern
The swell fools you in the dark; a hard impact runs up the keel.
You cut behind the reef and come up leeward of the false signal.
You avoid the worst, but a rock tears away planks.

The winches pull together and the drydock clears.
Coordinate the winches
At a snowbound shipyard, two crews need the same drydock cleared before ice locks the rails. The foreman asks you to break the deadlock by backing one maneuver.
The Icebound Drydock
The sloop changes hands and becomes your ship at the market price.
Buy the sloop
The inspection confirms sound repairs, with no reason to rush.
Inspect the hull
The broker looks for another buyer as you leave the slips.
Walk away
Beside the slips, a broker must sell a repaired sloop before its owner sails away. The hull is sound, the price is posted, and several buyers are already circling.
A Sloop for Sale
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_brass_ba: You recover the case before it fills with water. The tuba returns dented but playable.
The band finally accepts that one instrument is not worth a second rescue.
You throw empty boxes overboard and find a dry place for the tuba.
During the transfer, a tuba case slips between the hulls. Three musicians want to go back for it while the ferry starts spinning again.
You send their position toward the coast and keep your deck clear.
You take the performers aboard and leave their cases tarped on the ferry.
You tow the entire ferry slowly while the brass section never stops playing.
A ferry of musicians drifts with its engine dead, brass instruments still raised. They are due in Samba City tonight and are already arguing whether instruments or passengers board first.
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_briss_cr: The crate bursts on the stones, but the lane is empty.
Let it drop
The dockers take the weight together and set it down without further damage.
Lower it by hand
You lighten the crate in place; its cargo can be moved in smaller loads.
Open the crate
The backup line holds, but the crate is still hanging at head height. The crane cannot lift it and the dock has to reopen.
The Hanging Crate
The upright kicks you back hard and the crate drops a meter.
The gantry stops moving before the load touches the dock.
You slow the movement, but a beam splits under the strain.
You brace the gantry long enough for dockers to regain the cable.
Brace the gantry
The cable lashes the dock and cuts your forearm.
You freeze the load before it swings across the dock lane.
You catch the guide, but the crate slams into a stack of barrels.
You recover the guide and stop the crate from building momentum.
Grab the guide rope
You push bystanders back and let the crate fall into an empty patch.
Clear the dock
At Briss Port, a crane cable snaps over a busy lane. A suspended crate starts sweeping across the dock while workers scramble for a second guide.
Snapped Cable
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_centaure: Your tone hardens the office and the merchants lose their last chance to appeal.
The office suspends the entire hold until the records are checked.
The supervisor hears you without reopening the gates.
You get ten minutes to compare both ledgers.
You leave the office and let merchants settle the mismatch without you.
You blame the wrong column and get two innocent cargoes blocked.
You prove the error before guards shut down the whole dock.
You find the mismatch, but too late to save the day’s sale.
You trace the mismatch to one line copied twice.
In a South Blue city port, the royal office and dockworkers show two different totals for the same cargo. Guards are already closing the gates as merchants protest.
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_cold_por: You win a damaged lot nobody wanted to load in the snow.
You help sellers cover the lots before the next gust.
You spot the crates that took water before freezing and avoid a bad purchase.
You leave the auction to the cold and walk away without cargo.
In a cold South Blue market square, crates from warmer ports are being sold before frost damages them further. Buyers are already tapping boards to listen for frozen water inside.
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_crosscur: A long line is enough for them to reform.
Leave a stout line
The lane is clear; you leave the fishers to reset their nets.
Move on
You tow the skiff out of traffic into calm water.
Take a skiff in tow
One skiff keeps spinning in the current. Its skipper shouts that he only needs a solid pull to get out of traffic.
The Last Skiff
The knife slips: you cut your palm and the net stays caught.
You even recover the line and toss it back to the fishers.
You free the hull late and lose a few planks.
The net drops cleanly before it tears at the rudder.
Cut the outer net
You stop dead. The fishers clear the lane themselves, but the convoy loses its lead.
Heave to
Your wake rolls a skiff and its cargo spills overboard.
You guide the whole group clear without losing a crate.
You avoid the collision, but the nets rake the hull.
You open a clean lane through the lines.
Thread between the skiffs
Three fishing skiffs drift across a merchant current. Their nets are already catching your hull while another ship closes from behind: the lane has to open now.
Nets Across the Lane
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_drifting: You cut loose the worst-positioned barge to keep the others out of the current.
Sacrifice one barge
You focus on the harvest; the barges will have to be recovered later.
Save the baskets
You accept the delay and tow the barges toward a safer lane.
Tow the whole train

The Impossible Tow
You come in too fast: the bow crushes baskets on the first barge.
You recover the lead barge and line the others up behind it.
You catch the barge, but the impact damages your side.
You take the barge in tow before it drifts offshore.
Catch the lead barge
You miss the rail and fall hard between the hulls.
You cross barge to barge and secure the whole train.
You get the line on, but split your knee on a crate.
The towline bites in the right place and stops the drift.
Jump with a towline
You note heading and speed, then signal the barges to the next crew you meet.
Mark their drift

Harvest Adrift
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_forest_m: You refuse medicine you do not need and leave the stock for the village.
You pay for the preparation and let the clinic keep its supplies.
You help sort leaves and leave with advice instead of a debt.
In a South Blue forest village, a clinic lacks hands more than leaves. The herbalist offers travelers a simple exchange: one hour sorting herbs for one preparation.
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_harbor_n: You spend the evening filling basins and free the staff to treat patients.
You leave the staff to work without adding one more body to the corridor.
You pay a runner to fetch clean linen and save the clinic time.
You help separate emergencies from injuries that can wait.
In a South Blue port, the clinic receives injured dockers and two feverish sailors at once. What the staff lacks most is hands to move water, linen, and patients.
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_icewake_: You leave the area before another slab breaks loose.
Get clear fast
You mark the water’s motion before it vanishes under the ice.
Mark the counter-current
Your signal turns the following vessel away before the gap fully closes.
Warn the ship astern

The Blue Gap
You refuse the lane and take the longer route toward clearer water.
Back away from the ice
The rudder slips and the bow bites the ice.
You use the ice itself to turn without losing speed.
You make it through, but a floe scrapes the hull for several seconds.
The ship swings through just before the lane closes.
Force the turn
You mistake a shadow for a lane: the hull hits a submerged slab.
You also spot the counter-current that will close the lane behind you.
You find the opening, but too late to avoid a side impact.
The real lane appears between two floes.
Read the blue water
A cold South Blue current carries floes into the merchant route. Ahead, the opening is closing faster than expected and the hull has no room to spare.
Icewake
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_jewel_wh: Eight months later, a dispatch tells you the caravan changed its ropes and shelters after the squall.
Read the dispatch
You send back what you remember about where visibility broke down.
Send your notes
Eight months after the whiteout, a courier from South Blue’s cold routes finds you. The guides want to confirm what they changed after the accident.
Dispatch from the Cold
The guides send a small fee for helping shape their new procedures.
Accept their fee
You refuse to put your name on a shelter maintained by others.
Decline the plaque
Sixteen months after the accident, a new shelter opens on the route. The guides want to settle your part in the story before the next winter.
The Next Shelter
You build a low snow wall and wait for the whiteout to lift before moving.
Build a snow wall
You slip with the injured traveler and both hit the ice.
You keep enough strength to go back for a second person.
You make progress, but the effort drains you before shelter.
You carry the injured traveler into shelter.
Carry the injured
You lose the rope and walk to the lip of a crevasse before backing away.
You spot a break in the shelf and turn the whole group before it gives way.
You find the group after a long loop that freezes your hands.
You keep the rope at the right angle all the way to shelter.
Follow the rope

Whiteout
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_karate_o: You arrange another day instead of turning practice into a brawl.

Bow cleanly

The Last Bow
You drive straight in and hit the floor with the wind knocked out of you.
You control the center without hitting harder than needed.
You stay in the exchange, but take a clean hit to the ribs.
You set your base and force your opponent out of the ring.
Take the center
You watch the bout and learn where fighters lose balance.
Watch a round
You slide out of the ring and twist your ankle.
You win without letting your opponent touch center once.
You dodge the blows but eventually step out yourself.
You rotate the exchange until the other fighter steps out.
Work the edge

Open Mat
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_kutsukku: You note the spacing of the marks and learn to read their improvised shoals.
You give the poles a wide berth and leave the fishers to reset their own markers.
You stand several poles back up and the lane becomes readable again for small coasters.
Near a small South Blue island, fishers mark shoals with long painted poles. The swell has knocked several flat and the markers now point toward the wrong lane.
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_lantern_: You keep the last log. South Blue will keep ringing without you.
Keep the last note
You send the notes back with the next ship bound for South Blue.
Send the log back
You left South Blue before the next meeting. A courier hands you the last relay log: local keepers are taking the chain back without you.
The Last Bell
You leave the network to the pilots who actually know the channels.
Let the pilots run it
You push for a shared roster every port can inspect.
Publish the roster
You refuse to become keeper of a coastal system that is not yours.
Walk away

One Winter Later
You have sensitive routes masked from smugglers and cargo hunters.
Hide sensitive routes
The ports keep the roster open despite protests from the most powerful.
Keep names open

The Open Roster
The pilots accept one minimum shared code without giving up their local charts.
Set one common rule
Each port keeps its habits; you require only one universal stop signal.
Trust the ports

Pilots Among Themselves

Leave the chain

Darken one stretch
You help the ports bring enough stations back into agreement to save the season.
Repair the chain

The Broken Chain
You push merchant ports to jointly fund the stations they all use.
Share the cost
You accept a network paid by captains who want maintained signals.
Charge for passage
You refuse a common fund; only stations able to survive on volunteer work will remain.
Keep it voluntary
The network is working again, but maintenance costs more than emergency repairs. The ports now argue over the bill instead of the code.
Who Pays for the Light?
You leave the roster with a stable chain and keepers able to run it without you.
Hand it to locals
The bells remain a shared South Blue service. Your name stays in the earliest corrected logs.
Leave the network open

Open Lights
You force a fee low enough for small coasters to keep using the lights.
Cap the fee
You take your share of the proceeds and let the ports handle the criticism.
Take your share

Paid Lights

Break the rhythm

Correct the code

Record the mistake

You anchor until the lanterns finally agree.
Anchor and wait
You overestimate the channel and the hull hits bottom hard.
You cut a line clean enough for two ships behind to copy it.
You make it through without signals, but scrape bottom for several seconds.
You hold a safe line until a reliable light returns.
Navigate dark
You follow the wrong rhythm and skim a shoal before realizing the error.
You also identify which coastal station reversed its code.
You identify the faulty bell after a detour that shakes the hull.
You recover the true sequence among the conflicting signals.
Triangulate the bells
In South Blue fog, three coastal bells give incompatible bearings. A coaster behind you is already following the wrong rhythm toward an unseen shoal.
Bells in the Fog
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_market_b: You buy the lot before the bell and keep it from going back into storage.
You connect the farmer with a passing cook before closing.
You repack the crop properly so it survives until the next market.
The bell rings and the lot goes back to the cart.
At a South Blue farm market, the closing bell is about to ring and one grower still has a full lot unsold. Storage will cost nearly as much as the sale.
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_medicine: You give the doctor back the deck and keep your course.
Give the deck back
You keep one fragile crate sheltered until the next dock.
Keep one crate dry

Treat their deckhand

You cut too close to a shoal and the escort takes a hard hit.
You save enough time for the doctor to treat an injured passenger underway.
You keep the medical boat moving, at the cost of a collision with your hull.
You give it a stable route to the next harbor.
Clear the route
You copy their signal and pass it to ships you meet; the route opens slowly.
Relay the flag
A crate breaks between the hulls and injures your ankle.
You organize the transfer fast enough for the medical boat to depart light.
You save most of the crates, but two go overboard.
The medicine crosses safely onto your deck.
Transfer the crates

Medical Flag

Accept their thanks
You send the reward back to the clinic. Your name starts circulating among medical crews.
Send the money back
Six months later, a courier finds you with the medical boat’s receipt. The clinic wants to settle what it now considers a debt to you.
The Baterilla Receipt
You refuse to turn it into a lasting debt. The story ends on a clean salute.
Close the account
The courier gives you the latest habits of South Blue medical boats; you know better where to look for help.
Take the route notes
A second message arrives: the clinic turned your help into a habit and now passes your name among its visiting captains.
One Route Stays Open
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_mira_emp: {{npc_mira}} accepts a berth and joins your crew.
You spend an hour comparing recent South Blue routes without discussing commitment.
You let {{npc_mira}} look for another deck and keep the relationship intact.
At a South Blue recruitment port, {{npc_mira}} studies departure notices posted by the docks. She recognizes you and asks one simple question: does your next course need a real navigator?
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_port_din: You pay market price for the dinghy and leave with a simple boat.
You find two honest repairs and no reason to rush.
You let the bidding continue without raising a hand.
On a South Blue trade quay, three small dinghies are being sold as-is after inspection. One is clean enough to leave today if someone pays cash.
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_redfin_f: The trader offers you a share so the queue forgets the second weighing.

You accuse the wrong plate and the whole counter laughs.
You expose the trick before the whole queue without giving the merchant time to hide it.
You sense the fraud but cannot show where it hides.
You spot the hollow weight hidden under the plate.
Spot the false weight
The queue turns on you and two men shove you away from the counter.
The merchant takes his own scale apart before the crowd does it for him.
A few customers listen, but nobody wants to be first to protest.
The queue demands a second weighing for every sack.
Turn the queue
You leave the line and refuse to play with a scale nobody wants checked.
Refuse the price

Redfin Scales
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_redfin_s: Five months later, two Redfin men find you: the trader lost several customers and wants the account settled.
Face the collectors

Redfin’s Account

Buy peace

Spread the story

Close it without paying

A Weightless Debt
Your bluff rings false; the skiffs close in, certain they have a target.
They bolt before you finish your fake inspection.
They hesitate without leaving and keep you under watch.
A fake procedure shouted through a speaking trumpet is enough to scatter them.
Bluff a patrol
You cut too deep and scrape bottom before getting out.
You send them around a false lane and vanish behind a headland.
You lose them, but not before striking a shoal.

Lose them in shoals
You make a clean course change and deny them the excuse for an encounter.

Redfin Skiffs
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_royal_co: You shorten sail and let them settle their battle of protocol ahead of you.
Both cutters refuse to yield and squeeze you between their wakes.
Your line forces both captains to keep the same distance.
You get through, but one courier clips your side at the last moment.
You hold course and both cutters finally give way.
Your challenge triggers a volley of insults and one cutter crowds your hull.
Both couriers salute before reforming into a clean line.
They ignore you and continue their contest of precedence.
You make their quarrel look ridiculous enough that they slow down.

event.active_blue_south_blue_01_royal_ta: You make them compare receipts before the cart leaves. Two sacks have no matching line.
You help finish the loading and keep the argument from blocking the whole square.
You publicly back the sellers and force the collector to explain each seizure.
You refuse to enter a tax dispute that is not yours.
In a South Blue kingdom, a royal collector loads sacks directly onto a cart bearing the local seal. Three sellers insist they already paid the same levy.
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_samba_pa: The band covers the chaos and turns the evacuation into another part of the show.

One clear command opens the lane.
Clear the crowd
You cut the cloth jamming the wheel; the float loses its decoration but regains control.
Cut the banner
The drawbar knocks you down and the float crashes into a row of chairs.
You straighten the float without even breaking the parade rhythm.
You slow the float, but a wheel crushes part of the set.
You put the float back on line before it reaches the crowd.
Steer the float

Float Gone Sideways

Ask for a fee

Invitation from Samba

event.active_blue_south_blue_01_seventy_: You refuse to touch the crate and return it to base procedure.

event.active_blue_south_blue_01_smoke_ov: You alter course and later find a coastal trader heating tar on its hull. Nothing was burning.

event.active_blue_south_blue_01_sorbet_l: You ask for no name to be added to the report. The fix stays the yard’s work.

You slow the hull, but a support snaps under the load.
You hold long enough for the workers to reset a wedge.
Brace the keel

Tide Window
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_southpor: You pay market price and the yard prepares the sloop under your name.
Buy the sloop

Inspect the hull

Mark the fault

You stay outside the trial zone and let the shipwrights learn on their own.
Watch from a distance
The prototype turns sharper than expected and your side takes the hit.

You hold pace, but a close crossing damages both hulls.
You stay close enough to flag every flaw.
Match the trial hull

You spot the twist before it becomes a real break.
Read the hull

Trial Hull

Lift the gate

You limit the damage without saving the first crop.
You divert the overflow into an empty ditch.
Read the flow

event.active_blue_south_blue_01_torino_c: You let the herbalist decide and keep your hands away from a second mistake.
Let the herbalist decide

Compare the scent

You reach the canopy, but cut yourself on the way.
You gather dry leaves just before the rain.
Climb above the rain

Cover the baskets

Leaves Before Rain
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_winter_g: You sacrifice a piece of cargo timber to brace the deck.

Save the lashings

You leave the families to settle tomorrow’s catch among themselves.
Refuse to choose a boat
You spend the afternoon helping reinforce the shared net before the tide turns.
Mend the weakest sections
Your shipwright shows the fishers a faster splice and gets a second net usable by sunset.
Put your shipwright on it
Three fishing families spread one usable net across the beach. Each boat needs it at dawn, but there is not enough cord left to repair the other two.
One Net for Three Boats
You cover 2,000 Berrys for medicine so the entire catch can feed the village.
Pay for the clinic yourself
Every household receives food tonight, but no money is set aside for the clinic.
Divide it by household
The village keeps less food but sets aside money for the next medical purchase.
Sell a portion for medicine
You step away before the catch is divided and let the fishers settle it.
Leave the argument alone
A small boat returns with a rare heavy catch after several empty days. Before the fish are unloaded, hungry households argue over whether to divide them or sell enough for medicine.
The Shared Catch
The houses empty slowly enough for families to recover blankets and tools.
Join the bucket line
You sit out the last minutes of the emergency and keep the injury from worsening.
Stop and bind your wounds
You move the driest sacks uphill before seawater ruins the village’s reserve.
Save the grain sacks
The first rush is contained, but the flooded houses keep filling from below. Someone shouts for a bucket line while another group tries to save sacks of grain.
The Bucket Line
A loose block rolls over your leg and the breach widens before anyone can reset it.
You lock two fallen slabs together and turn the worst current away from the houses.
You hold one slab briefly, but the current forces everyone back.
You wedge the largest slab long enough for villagers to pack smaller stones behind it.
Brace the broken wall
You help the youngest villagers reach high ground while others fight the breach.
Carry children uphill
You slip in the wash and hit a doorpost while one family abandons its supplies.
You clear all three houses and save the dry food stored under the rafters.
You reach one house, but the second is already ankle-deep in water.
You get the nearest families outside before the water reaches their sleeping mats.
Race the flood to the houses
A section of Sphinx’s rough stone tidewall collapses as the sea rises. Water pours toward three low houses while villagers drag baskets and children uphill.
The Tidewall Gives Way
event.active_new_world_frontier_b_01_sto: The yard seals the worst seam quickly and sends you away before the berth dispute begins.
Take the cheap patch
You keep your Berrys and clear the alley before the rival crew arrives.
Leave before paying
You pay 2,500 Berrys and the yard completes a solid repair before the rival crew arrives.
Pay the rush fee
Your shipwright rejects the worst shortcuts and turns the patch into a dependable repair.
Have your shipwright supervise
A back-alley yard offers to patch your ship before nightfall, no questions asked. The foreman wants cash up front and warns that a rival crew may claim the berth.
The Black-Sail Repair Yard
You settle the ownership and walk away before learning what the crate contains.
Refuse the money
You refuse to arbitrate contraband and force both crews to clear the table elsewhere.
Make both crews leave
You accept 1,500 Berrys and make the owner remove the crate from the dock immediately.
Take the settlement fee
A tavern keeper drags out a scarred table and demands the crate be settled there, not with blades. The real owner offers a fee if you finish the dispute.
The Claims Table
You trust a rehearsed detail and hand leverage to the more dangerous crew.
You expose a planted lie and make the false claim collapse in front of the dock.
Both stories contain enough truth to keep the standoff alive.
You catch a detail only the real owner could know about the crate’s bindings.
Read the two stories
You make it clear the box is not yours and leave the two crews to settle their claim.
Step away from the crate
Your warning is taken as a challenge and someone smashes you into the crate.
The dock turns against anyone who starts violence, and both crews accept a neutral check.
The weapons lower, but neither crew agrees to leave without a ruling.
You force both crews to name terms instead of reaching for weapons.
Talk both crews down
A dock porter drops an unmarked black crate beside your baggage, then vanishes into the crowd. Two armed crews immediately arrive, each claiming the box belongs to them.
The Wrong Black Crate
You stay under the cliff but keep enough eyes on the mooring lines that nobody approaches unnoticed.
Keep the berth and double watch
You keep the cheap sheltered berth and trust that the warning was meant for someone else.
Ignore the warning
You pay 1,000 Berrys for a noisier public berth and leave the sheltered cliff before dark.
Move to the open quay
Your navigator identifies a safer anchor angle that makes a cut line less likely to send the ship onto rocks.
Ask your navigator to inspect currents
A scarred fisher quietly warns that ships moored under the eastern cliff are cut loose after midnight. Your berth is cheap, sheltered, and exactly where they are pointing.
The Quiet Anchorage Warning
You tear up the false fee book so it cannot be reused to legitimize another shakedown.
Destroy the ledger
The carriers use the names and amounts to organize their own claims against the collectors.
Return the ledger to the carriers
A local broker pays 1,000 Berrys for the names and disappears with the book.
Sell the ledger to a broker
One watchman drops the fee ledger while leaving. Several paid carriers point to their names and ask whether the money can still be recovered.
A Worthless Receipt
They surround you, take 1,000 Berrys by force, and send you through under jeers.
The watchmen lose the crowd completely and abandon the lane before a fight starts.
They lower the price but keep the lane blocked for everyone else.
The waiting carriers refuse to pay once someone openly challenges the watchmen.
Call their bluff
You hand over 750 Berrys and move through while the watchmen keep collecting behind you.
Pay and pass
You point to a real mark by mistake and give the watchmen room to mock the accusation.
You expose every stamp as recycled fraud and the whole queue refuses to pay.
You prove the stamps are inconsistent, but the men still control the lane.
You identify copied marks from unrelated docks and turn the waiting carriers against the fee.
Expose the fake stamps
You turn away from the shakedown and lose time circling the warehouses.
Take another lane
Three self-appointed harbor watchmen block a warehouse lane and demand a protection fee from everyone carrying goods. Their ledger has official-looking stamps, but none match.
The Harbor Watch Fee
The ship least able to relocate takes the first load; the remaining water goes by queue order.
Serve the damaged ship first
You step away once the line is restored and let the pump owner choose who waits.
Leave the choice to the owner
Two small crews fill their casks while the largest ship waits for morning.
Serve the smaller crews first
The cutters finally step back, but the pump has lost pressure during the argument. Only two full loads can be drawn before dark.
Who Pumps First
You leave the pump to its protection arrangement and pay 1,000 Berrys for casks from a private seller.
Buy water elsewhere
The crew laughs, shoves you into the pump frame, and keeps the front position.
The entire quay backs the original order, leaving the pirate crew isolated without a fight.
They stop pushing forward but refuse to move their barrels.
Other crews back your demand and the cutters lose the front position.
Hold the line verbally
A barrel clips your knee and a pirate answers with a hard shove.
You clear the whole lane so quickly that the waiting dockhands close ranks behind you.
You move one barrel, but the crew blocks the rest.
You roll the barrels out of the queue before the crew can surround you.
Roll their barrels aside
A freshwater pump serves three ships before dusk. A pirate crew cuts the line with empty barrels while dockhands mutter that the pump owner pays protection to them.
The Pump Line
event.active_new_world_frontier_b_01_yuk: The crate disappears under the shelf, but nobody risks the unstable edge again.
Cut the rope
You haul the crate up and preserve the expedition’s measurements.
Recover the instruments
The survey leader pays 1,000 Berrys for the risky recovery and gets the instruments back.
Ask for a recovery fee
Everyone reaches stable ice, but one survey crate hangs from the last rope over black water. The instruments are valuable; the shelf edge is still cracking.
One Rope Left
The surface drops under one foot and you slam onto the ice before scrambling free.
You find a narrow pressure ridge that lets everyone cross without losing the sled.
You reach one surveyor but must abandon the sled as the crack opens.
You guide both surveyors over the thinnest section before it separates.
Cross light and fast
The surveyors reach stable ice while their equipment slides away with the breaking shelf.
Cut the sled loose
The rope jerks you onto the ice and the sled drops one crate into the crack.
You wrench the whole load clear just before the shelf breaks away behind it.
You move the sled only halfway before the shelf shifts again.
You drag the sled and both surveyors onto stable ice.
Haul the sled across
A blue crack races across the ice shelf beneath two surveyors and their sled. The shore is close, but the split widens with every wave under the ice.
The Shelf Cracks
You keep to the mapped route and let the smoke vanish behind the ridge.
Avoid the unknown camp
You find stranded travelers burning damp driftwood and show them the safest route back.
Follow the smoke
You mark a path from the ridge so whoever made the fire can reach the main trail.
Leave route markers
A thin smoke column rises from a remote inlet where no expedition camp is marked. Snow will cover the tracks by evening, and the nearest shelter is hours away.
Smoke Beyond the Ridge
You repack the cache and raise its marker above the new snowline.
Reseal it for the team
Your navigator adds a precise bearing and date, making the cache easier to recover later.
Ask your navigator to update the marker
You treat the missing team as gone and take what the weather has not ruined.
Strip the abandoned cache
You take enough fuel to weather the coming storm and leave the food and rope intact.
Take only dry fuel
An old expedition cache emerges from melting snow: rope, dry fuel and sealed rations. The marker names a team months overdue, and a storm front is approaching.
The Half-Buried Cache
You leave the old case untouched and use the shelf only to wait out the surge.
Leave it where it is
You scratch a clear tide mark for future travelers before moving on.
Mark the safe shelf
You carry the case out and later return it to the expedition camp for a small reward.
Take the map case
Halfway through, the cave opens onto a dry shelf littered with old expedition pegs and a sealed tin map case. The next surge can be heard outside.
A Dry Shelf
You mistake old storm stains for the normal high line and linger too long.
You identify a dry shelf that makes the entire crossing safer for the group.
You confirm the cave floods fast but cannot judge the safe window precisely.
The stain layers reveal which tunnel remains above water longest.
Read the water stains
You reject the cave and lose most of the day to the exposed headland trail.
Take the long headland route
You enter on the wrong surge and a wave throws you against the cave wall.
You read the full tide rhythm and cross with enough time to inspect a side chamber safely.
You mistime the lull and have to retreat soaked before the narrowest section.
You catch the correct lull and cross before the next surge fills the tunnel.
Time the crossing
A guide points to a sea cave that opens only between two violent tides. Inside lies a shortcut across the headland, but the waterline is already climbing.
The Tide Cave Window
You carve a lower but durable direction mark into the exposed rock.
Score the rocks instead
You rebuild the marker high enough to remain visible through the next snowfall.
Repair the marker
You leave the broken pole and get the expedition back across the beach before the channel fills.
Return before the tide
The return line reappears, but its final pole has snapped near a tidal channel. The group can repair it for future travelers or hurry back before the water closes the beach.
The Last Marker
You mistake a wind-carved hollow for the return line and lead everyone toward a flooded inlet.
You find both the marker line and a sheltered descent the expedition missed on the way out.
You recover the general direction, but the group loses time crossing bad ground.
You match the wind to the ridge shape and recover the missing marker line.
Read wind and slope
The group shelters behind packed snow until visibility improves, losing the rest of the day.
Dig in and wait
You chase a dark shape that is only ice and expose the group to the wind.
You uncover an old expedition mark pointing to a safer route above the tide.
You find one broken cairn but cannot tell which direction it once marked.
A line of half-buried stones leads back toward the camp.
Search for old cairns
Your navigator reconstructs the return line from the wind and shore angle.
Let your navigator lead
A coastal expedition loses sight of its return markers as snow blows sideways. The tide is rising behind the group, and the camp cannot be seen from the ridge.
Markers in the Whiteout
event.active_new_world_route_start_mysto: You rise beyond the Red Line and follow the current toward Mystoria Island.
At Fish-Man Island, one New World needle settles on Mystoria Island. A deep current offers a clean line forward.
event.active_new_world_route_start_raiji: You rise beyond the Red Line and take the stormbound course toward Raijin Island.
At Fish-Man Island, one New World needle locks onto Raijin Island. The bearing promises violent weather.

event.active_paradise_p1_classic_01_alab: Packed sand around the stakes keeps the remaining canvas down.
Bury the stakes
The group abandons the canvas and waits out the gust behind the axles.
Move behind the carts
The canvas tears free of your hands and a frame hits you before flying into the sand.
You use the wind to fold the whole structure cleanly without losing a single rope.
You hold one side, but two families lose their shade in the gust.
You pull the canvas flat and pin the corners before the next blast hits.
Pin the canvas
A sandstorm hits a caravan stop and tears loose the large shade canvas. Families crouch behind carts while the stakes pull out of the ground one by one.
Canvas in the Wind
The number matches the ledger; the clerk corrects the seal without seizing the cargo.
Compare the ledger
You pass the checkpoint while the two men continue arguing.
Leave the dispute
The goods stay cool while the merchant fixes the paperwork.
Shade the cargo
A clerk stops a cart at a checkpoint because its transport seal is stamped upside down. The merchant swears another office cleared it, but the sun is beginning to spoil the cargo.
The Reversed Seal
The family fills the canteen without reducing the shared reserve.
Give your ration
The keeper measures everyone equally and finds enough margin for the child.
Measure every canteen
The rule holds, but the family leaves with only its original ration.
Respect the queue

One Canteen Too Many
The keeper closes the channel and accepts a lost day to avoid permanent damage.
Close for repairs
You force the wrong gate and water spills into a secondary canal that is already full.
You also reset the worn stop, preventing the gate from jamming on the next cycle.
You free part of the mechanism, but the flow remains too weak to satisfy the line.
You spot the stone jammed under the rack and restore the main channel.
Inspect the rack
All three plots receive less water, but none is completely cut off.
Share the weak flow
An irrigation gate refuses to open while three farmers wait for their water turn. The keeper fears breaking the rack, and each farmer already blames the previous one for forcing it.
The Jammed Sluice
You choose a track that is too fresh and lead the cart into deeper sand.
You spot a nearly invisible gravel strip that saves the whole caravan hours.
You find a way through, but a wheel sinks and half the sacks must be unloaded.
You read the older ruts and guide the cart over the firmest ground.
Find firm ground
You plant markers toward a longer but passable loop.
Mark a detour
The sacks move by hand and the cart rises enough to roll again.
Unload the cart
A date cart sinks to its axle on a road erased by wind. The next caravan is approaching and cannot pass around it without entering soft dunes.
Axle in the Sand
event.active_paradise_p1_classic_01_cact: You turn the marker onto the wrong bearing; a fisher shouts before correcting your mistake.
You also find a second mark carved underneath for ships coming from Reverse Mountain.
The current hides the clue and you cannot prove which way the board should point.
Salt deposits and brush strokes reveal the marker's original direction.
Inspect the traces
You mark the rock so the next crew checks the board before trusting its bearing.
Add a warning
You reset the board as the fisher says and note the symbol painted on its back.
Trust the fisher
On a rocky point, a painted board marks the coastal current in the wrong direction. A fisher says someone turned it overnight, just before several ships arrived.
The Backward Marker
You misread the gauge and open an almost empty valve, drawing shouts from the whole line.
You find a hidden leak; fixing it restores enough water to calm both lines.
Your estimate convinces nobody and the argument keeps the cistern blocked.
You spot a secondary line that is still full and split the wait between two taps.
Read the gauge
Each line gets a reduced ration and the cistern lasts until evening.
Propose a split
Your group steps back; the tension falls, but you will need to find water elsewhere.
Yield your turn
At the harbor cistern, locals refuse to serve a crew that arrived before dawn. The gauge is falling fast, and two lines begin shoving around the same valve.
The Contested Cistern
You wedge a beam under the bollard and the dockhands slowly haul the skiff back.
Brace the mooring
The line lashes your face and the skiff hits the rocks before anyone regains it.
You recover the skiff and secure the neighboring moorings too.
You catch the line too late; several crates end up in the water.
You pin the skiff against the pier before the gust can take it again.
Grab the line
A few crates are sacrificed, but the skiff stops dragging the line.
Cut loose the crates

Skiff in the Thorns
The shed comes down before the flames reach it, creating a second fuel break.
Pull down the shed
The watchmen let the empty shed burn and keep the water for the fire line.
Save the water for the line
The soaked rope refuses to catch when sparks arrive.
Soak the rope
The firebreak is barely holding when the wind shifts and drives the flames toward a shed packed with dry rope. The watchmen have only one barrel of water within reach.
The Wind Turns
You clear scrub around the stores and the fire runs out of fuel.
Dig a firebreak
More hands arrive quickly enough to hold the fire line.
Ring the harbor bell
The watchmen move the jars while the fire burns only across the ridge.
Save the water stores
A signal fire jumps its stone ring and catches dry scrub. Watchmen haul buckets from the harbor, but the wind is already driving flames toward their stores.
Fire on the Ridge
Vendors lend their brooms and the lane reopens before a child is hurt.
Sweep the spines
The porter admits the strap snapped; the sabotage accusation dies down.
Question the porter
You skirt the dispute and reach the pier without getting involved.
Take the back lane
A basket of cactus pulp bursts in the market lane. Spines roll under sandals, a vendor accuses a sailor of sabotage, and the crowd blocks the only path to the pier.
The Thorn Market
event.active_paradise_p1_classic_01_drum: You block the snow and give the staff enough calm to work.
Hold the door
The crew Medic takes over triage and assigns places without wasting time.
Let the Medic lead
You misclassify two symptoms and the clinic loses precious minutes correcting the order.
You reorganize the room so cleanly that the staff free a bed before the next sled arrives.
Your triage reduces the crush but does not solve the bed shortage.
You clearly separate cold emergencies from mechanical injuries and speed up treatment.
Triage the patients
A mountain clinic receives three patients almost at once: frostbite, a broken leg, and fever. Only one table is free, relatives all talk at once, and snow blows through the door.
The Full Clinic
You block access and send the line toward a longer but safer detour.
Close the bridge
The ice breaks under your step and you drop waist-deep into black water.
You find a line of old ice that even lets the baskets cross without overloading it.
You reach the middle, but villagers must abandon their baskets to retreat.
You stagger the crossings so no two heavy loads share the same ice plate.
Guide the crossings
The loads stay on the bank while the villagers cross lighter.
Unload the baskets

The Ice Bridge
Everyone gets out before the awning collapses onto the tables.
Clear the stalls
Two emergency posts hold long enough to clear the snow.
Prop the beam

Save the common cashbox

The Overloaded Awning
One crate vanishes under snow, but the carriers keep the rest.
Abandon the outer crate

Drag the crates under rock
Everyone shelters behind the sled until the slide passes.
Shield the carriers
Another rumble starts above the sled. The second slide is smaller, but it is aimed at the shelf where the carriers set the rescued crates.
The Second Slide
You brace too low; the snow sweeps you away with the sled for several meters.
You also clear a safe pocket where the carriers can wait out the slides.
You slow the sled, but a second wave of snow pins it beneath a ledge.
You take the slope at an angle and guide the sled out of the avalanche chute.
Brace the sled
The carriers abandon the heaviest crates and save the rest of the medicine.
Split the load
Villagers climb up with ropes before the slope moves again.
Signal the village

The Medicine Sled
The crew Navigator cross-checks the terrain and brings you back onto the marked line.
Follow the Navigator
The strips remain visible at hand height even after snow covers the stakes.
Tie cloth markers
You lead the travelers back to harbor before visibility worsens.
Walk them back
A whiteout erases the red stakes marking the path from harbor to high ground. Travelers circle the same rock while their tracks disappear behind them.
Markers in the Whiteout
event.active_paradise_p1_classic_01_jaya: The crowd backs under awnings before the largest debris lands.
Clear the quay
Drivers pull their carts out of the area and clear the lane.
Move the carts
You note unusual shells and wear marks before salvagers take everything.
Study the debris
An upward current bursts offshore and rains pieces of wood, fish, and a cracked bell onto the harbor. Bystanders stare upward instead of leaving the falling zone.
Rain from Above
You trust the cleanest drawing, which happens to copy a false current legend.
You find a coastal detail absent from originals and identify the table where the copies were altered.
You prove the charts contradict each other without determining which was copied first.
The same scale errors appear across several sheets and reveal a single workshop.
Compare the scales
You keep only the useful annotations for comparison without trusting the drawn route.
Keep one as a clue
The crews pocket their money and the seller folds his table under boos.
Warn the buyers
A vendor sells charts supposedly showing rising currents toward the sky. Three crews compare their purchases and find islands drawn in different places on every copy.
Charts of the Sky
A plank gives way and you finish hanging from a halyard under the dock's laughter.
You touch the mark, climb down cleanly, and turn the wager back on the one who challenged you.
You reach the mast, but your rival touches the mark first.
You use the ship's roll to gain the last length of rope.
Climb for the pennant
You tell an impossible exploit; the crowd forgets the race to argue over your lie.
Answer with a story
The sailor finds another challenger and the crowd drifts back toward the tavern.
Refuse the bet

Rigging Wager
The auctioneer repeats the rules loudly enough to draw nearby dockworkers.
Demand a public bid
You leave the locals to settle their power struggle without involving your crew.
Leave the auction
The lumber moves into a locked warehouse before any buyer is forced to yield.
Move the lot inside

The Rough Auction
The weight drops away and the partners haul the diver up more easily.
Cut the salvage bag
The crew Medic sets the pace and brings the diver up without rushing him.
Let the Medic take over
You pull too early: the rope burns your palms and the diver strikes the edge on the way up.
You recover both diver and bag without letting the rope foul beneath the pier.
You bring him back conscious, but his salvage bag sinks with the cut line.
You pace the ascent and the diver catches his breath before reaching the dock.
Pace the ascent
A salvage diver surfaces too quickly beside the pier and clings to his line without answering. His partners hesitate between hauling him up immediately or keeping him in the water a moment longer.
The Pale Diver
event.active_paradise_p1_classic_01_litt: The group follows its own tracks back before the parent appears.
Backtrack quietly
You let the massive shape pass between the trees without touching the nest.
Hide beneath the roots
A discreet marker will keep later travelers from taking this detour.
Mark the nest from afar
The detour opens onto a huge nest built between two roots. A cracked egg moves in the leaves while the roar heard earlier closes in behind the group.
At the Nest Edge
From a fallen trunk, you spot a longer loop back to camp.
Climb for a view
You mistake a fresh trail for a safe path and emerge in front of a predator that sends you running back.
You find a rise that also reveals the next dangerous area before you enter it.
You avoid the herd, but the detour keeps you away from camp for a long time.
The tracks reveal a recent opening that lets you cross between two animal passes.
Read the tracks
You let the herd pass and lose several hours, but no animal spots you.
Wait under cover
Trees shake ahead of camp, then a gigantic herd cuts across the only clear trail. Tracks overlap in the mud, and a closer roar announces something following the herbivores.
The Crushed Trail
A drainage cut diverts the water before it reaches the sleeping area.
Cut a drain
Your shove sends the wrong trunk moving and a mass of ferns crashes onto you.
You turn the fall into a stable walkway above the soaked undergrowth.
You clear a narrow gap, but camp remains cut off from its water source.
You identify the load-bearing trunk and open a corridor without bringing the rest down.
Find the load-bearing trunk
The camp retreats to drier ground and gives up the path for the day.
Move the tents

The Fallen Canopy
You lure the swarm away with one sack and save the remaining supplies.
Sacrifice one sack
The lids slam shut just before the swarm reaches the dry stores.
Seal every crate
Smoke drives the swarm off long enough to seal the stores.
Smoke the sacks
A cloud of fist-sized insects drops onto open food sacks. Cooks swat the air with lids while the first creatures are already tearing through the canvas.
The Hungry Cloud
You save the rest without risking the bank any further.
Abandon two barrels
The ground gives way under your feet and steam burns you before you can retreat.
You find a seam of cold rock that lets you recover the entire stock without nearing the steam.
You move one barrel, but two others remain cut off behind scalding water.
You roll the barrels over firm ground before the water rises.
Map the cold ground
The logs form a rough bridge and the barrels come back one by one.
Lay fallen logs
A pool that was warm moments ago starts boiling around the camp's water barrels. The ground steams, ropes soften, and nobody knows which part of the bank will collapse next.
The Boiling Pool
A new line secures the equipment and lets the surveyors return.
Anchor a new line
You mark the crossing as unsafe and give up on the hanging equipment.
Close the crossing
The surveyors abandon their instruments but leave the ravine alive.
Recover only the people

Bones over the Ravine
event.active_paradise_p1_classic_01_long: One skiff breaks free and the other two stop pulling against each other.
Cut one anchor line
The crew Helmsman gives all three pilots one order and untangles the circle.
Let the Helmsman call it
The pilots keep the hulls apart until the current weakens.
Wait for the turn

The Circular Current
You cheer for a local who knows every bump in the flats.
Back a local racer
You help move the finish line out of the first area the tide will cover.
Hold the finish line
You miss a step, hit the ground hard, and finish the race in a puddle under the cheers.
You finish far enough ahead that the locals offer you the starting ribbon as a trophy.
You keep pace, but the wind makes you miss the final pole.
You use the stilts' flex and clear the last stretch without breaking stride.
Race the stilts

The Stilt Race
The crew Navigator chooses the channel that will hold enough water longest.
Follow the Navigator
You read the wrong ripple and the tide surrounds the ferry before you reach the dry strip.
You find a deeper pass that lets the loaded ferry leave before the tide returns.
You free the ferry, but it must abandon part of its load on the sand.
You follow the receding current and pull the ferry into a channel that stays open long enough.
Read the returning tide
The ferry becomes light enough to push toward a shallow channel.
Unload the baskets

Ferry on the Flats
The tents collapse and the animal simply steps over the slack lines.
Drop the tents
The herd changes direction and gives the camp room to recover.
Throw food away
You pull at the wrong moment and a long leg sends you rolling through the grass.
You turn the lines into a wide loop and calmly guide the whole herd around the tents.
You free one rope, but the animal leaves with two stakes still attached.
You release tension one rope at a time and the animal gets out without tearing down camp.
Untangle line by line

Legs in the Lines
Several adults shove each cart through the mud to firm ground together.
Form a push line
The camp sacrifices gear and gets the carts moving before the route closes.
Leave the heavy poles
The children reach high ground while the adults finish loading.
Move the children first
A nomad camp delays packing until the tide begins closing the paths across the flats. The carts are still half loaded, and children gather animals that refuse to move.
Camp in the Tide
event.active_paradise_p1_classic_01_rout: The stitching shows which half was moved after the pennant was placed.
Compare the fabric
You only note the place and continue without trusting the marker.
Ignore the symbol
You stop the misleading pennant from turning further and leave a warning.
Tie both halves down
Two months later, a pennant bearing the same symbol hangs from a current marker. It has been cut in half, and each half now points toward a different channel.
The Split Pennant
The scratches retain enough pigment to reconstruct the old direction.
Copy the old outline
At least the marker stops giving a false bearing.
Leave the board bare
You replace the arrow with a symbol that simply tells crews to verify the current.
Paint a neutral warning
