Your legacy gives autonomy without removing accountability.
Your legacy sets protections that survive circumstances.
event.career_marine_10_moving_justice.te: High command wants a mobile force able to answer crises across regions without waiting on each local chain. Speed will gain days, but also concentrate great power in a few hands.
event.career_marine_10_ordered_justice_i: You refuse to let the scene die at local level.
The text remains usable even by those who dislike being checked.
You change the form without abandoning accountability.
Three admirals mark your draft in opposite directions. One wants more control, one more speed, and the third no rule that can be cited against command.
You keep your field of action without turning the doctrine into a stepping stone.
You choose to enforce the standard through daily decisions rather than a chair.
The doctrine is adopted in part. The council then asks whether you would carry ultimate responsibility for applying it, not merely for writing it.
event.career_marine_10_ordered_justice.c: Your legacy becomes a chain people can follow and check.
Your legacy gives autonomy without removing accountability.
Your legacy sets protections that survive circumstances.
event.career_marine_10_ordered_justice.t: After years of conflicting reports between bases, high command asks you for a common doctrine. It must survive weak officers, real emergencies, and the temptation to hide mistakes behind rank.
event.career_marine_10_white_coat.choice: Your legacy becomes a chain people can follow and check.
Your legacy gives autonomy without removing accountability.
Your legacy sets protections that survive circumstances.
event.career_marine_10_white_coat.text: At thirty-three, your file reaches the senior council: promotions, refusals, reports, and crises fill several stacks. You are finally asked what your service should leave behind.
event.career_marine_10_white_coat.title: The White Coat
event.career_marine_promotion_admiral.ch: The files pass under your responsibility: the Marines now count you among their Admirals.
event.career_marine_promotion_admiral.te: High command places three emergency files before you, each serious enough to mobilize forces beyond one region. A fourth document already bears your name and the proposed rank.
event.career_marine_promotion_captain.ch: The first order leaves under your seal: the Marines recognize you as a Captain.
event.career_marine_promotion_captain.te: The dispatch office brings you a command seal with a packet of unsigned orders. From now on, entire operations will carry your name before leaving the Marine chain of command.
The markers pass under your authority: your appointment as Commander takes effect.
Three conflicting reports cover an operations table. Command no longer asks for a recommendation: it places the unit markers under your hand and waits for your deployment order.
The first dispatches now carry your authority as a Commodore.
A dispatch case arrives with the pennants of several units. The message is brief: their commanders will now report at your level before their reports travel farther up the chain.
event.career_marine_promotion_fleet_admi: Fleet command is entered under your name; every order that follows will commit the institution as a whole.
The command room is empty except for files stacked before the central seat. The officers present are not offering a reward: they are waiting to learn under whose direction the Marines will now act.
event.career_marine_promotion_lieutenant: The commission is countersigned: you now serve as a Lieutenant.
A Marine courier brings a sealed commission into the debriefing. It formally places a unit under you and turns your decisions into recorded responsibility rather than field initiative alone.
event.career_marine_promotion_petty_offi: Your name enters the register as a Petty Officer; the next watch will wait for your instructions.
A superior closes the mission report and pushes the watch register toward you. Your name must now appear among those who assign people and answer for the orders they give.
event.career_marine_promotion_rear_admir: The chart becomes your theater of operations: you are promoted to Rear Admiral.
A chart is unrolled before you with several task groups already committed. The file is not asking for local advice: it assigns you responsibility for coordinating their next movements.
event.career_marine_promotion_vice_admir: The staff comes to attention: your promotion to Vice Admiral is entered into the record.
A priority Den Den Mushi rings while a staff waits around the table. The line is not carrying a mission: it grants you authority to commit an entire force.
event.career_pirate_01_first_flag_i01.ch: You sell the information to someone hungrier and keep your hands clean tonight.
You memorize the timing and leave before someone else claims the idea.
event.career_pirate_01_first_flag_i01.te: A drunk sailor drops a purse on the table: a corrupt collector carries his cashbox alone to the docks before dawn. The laughter stops; everyone waits for your reaction.
event.career_pirate_01_first_flag.choice: Your challenge rings hollow; the room laughs harder.
Even the owner stops wiping his glass; your name is already moving table to table.
A few heads turn, then the room resumes without you.
The room goes quiet long enough to remember your name.
You spell out what your flag will accept—and what it will never do for a prize.
You drink without answering. They laugh again, but none knows what you will do tomorrow.
event.career_pirate_01_first_flag.text: In a port tavern, three pirates laugh at your fresh flag: no great prize, no known name, maybe not even a ship. One slides a mug toward you and asks what you plan to take first.
event.career_pirate_01_first_flag.title: A Captain Without a Story
event.career_pirate_01_inherited_wake_i0: You refuse to let an inherited debt decide where you may walk.
You agree to talk, but only about a debt you personally recognize.
The smuggler lowers his voice: a rival crew still claims a debt tied to your family. They have just entered the port looking for the new captain.
event.career_pirate_01_inherited_wake.ch: You keep the inheritance to yourself and ask to be known only by your own flag.
You take up their words, but you decide when they apply.
You declare that your family name will not command your crew.
event.career_pirate_01_inherited_wake.te: At the quay, an old smuggler recognizes a mark from your family and hands you the rope of a seized skiff. “So, captain: do you carry their way of life, or invent your own?”
event.career_pirate_02_false_manifest_i0: You spread his false manifest through the docks and make your name too dangerous to borrow.
You take the money and leave him his trade, certain he now owes you a favor.
The cargo’s owner arrives furious: a small trafficker who thought your name was new enough to use as a mask. He offers to pay to make the affair disappear.
event.career_pirate_02_false_manifest.ch: You pay before the case climbs higher, then memorize the forged name for later.
You play their lie to the end and announce that if your name is on it, the cargo is yours.
You accuse the wrong dockworker; the real forger vanishes while the agents hold you.
You identify both the forger and the person who paid them before the agents understand the scheme.
You see the trail too late and have to pay your way out without proof.
The ink, fold, and a dock-number mistake lead you to the real forger’s office.
event.career_pirate_02_false_manifest.te: A port customs officer holds a sheet listing your name beside cargo you have never seen. Two agents close the exit behind you; someone is already using your reputation as cover.
event.career_pirate_02_first_story_sprea: You sign beneath your own portrait. The rookie label sticks, but the name spreads.
You tear down the image and let the waiter explain why nobody stopped you.
The printer pulls a still-wet proof and hands it to the nearby waiter. He points at your name under the drawing and asks whether “that captain” truly deserves to be feared.
You cross out useful lies along with flattering ones and impose your version.
You give him the biggest details, not necessarily the truest.
You refuse the story. Your silence becomes the sentence he prints.
A traveling printer shows you three versions of the same story: hero, brute, or swindler. He has not printed your name yet, but tomorrow he will sell what the docks think they know about you.
event.career_pirate_02_harbor_debt_i01.c: You take the money and promise your name will answer if the gang returns.
You push the cashbox back: their freedom will not become your new tax.
event.career_pirate_02_harbor_debt_i01.t: The gang leaves the market, but the fishmonger pushes a cashbox toward you. “If I pay someone now, I want to know what I’m buying.”
event.career_pirate_02_harbor_debt.choic: You enter their alley without seeing the man on the roof and retreat under a rain of stones.
You turn their own ambush against them; the district opens its shutters when you return.
You scatter them briefly, but they keep enough men to return tomorrow.
You break their collection and force them out of the market.
You name a clear price: less than the gang, but enough to make your flag a business.
You show them where to watch, when to raise the alarm, and how to refuse without calling you every week.
event.career_pirate_02_harbor_debt.text: A fishmonger closes her stall in front of you: an armed gang takes half the district’s catch every week. She knows you are a pirate, but still asks whether your flag is worth more than theirs.
event.career_pirate_02_harbor_debt.title: The Harbor's Debt
event.career_pirate_02_red_sail_toll_i01: You leave without raising your own chain. The boatmen will remember that detail.
You take a cut of the traffic; the channel merely changes masters.
The red-sail first mate promises their captain will remember your name. Behind him, the smaller crews wait to see whether you will collect the toll in his place.
event.career_pirate_02_red_sail_toll.cho: You strike too early; their men pin you against the quay.
You throw their chain into the water before the whole channel; nobody pays this morning.
You push them back, but leave bruised without breaking their toll.
Their blockade gives way long enough for the smaller boats to pass behind you.
You pay once and carve their symbol into your own list of debts.
You persuade the blocked crews to refuse the next collection together.
event.career_pirate_02_red_sail_toll.tex: A red-sailed sloop blocks the channel and charges every small crew a “passage toll.” Their first mate recognizes you, grins at your flag, then doubles the price only for you.
event.career_pirate_03_crew_draws_line_i: You refuse the contract and stake your name: your word will be the proof.
You put the rule in black and white; your crew will know what to measure your next decisions against.
Someone places a piece of charcoal beside the table. “Write it down. Next time, nobody gets to say they understood something else.”
event.career_pirate_03_crew_draws_line.c: Your voice rises too fast; the room closes off and nobody gives you the set-aside sack.
You turn the dispute into a pact: everyone recounts the sacks and confirms your rule.
You get your share, but the silence around the table costs more than the coins.
You set a rule everyone accepts for this score and the next ones.
You leave them the fourth sack and keep only what was agreed.
You take the same share as everyone else and make the rule a precedent.
event.career_pirate_03_crew_draws_line.t: After a profitable score, your crew sets three sacks on the table and keeps a fourth aside. Nobody threatens anyone yet; they want to know whether your share is worth more than theirs.
event.career_pirate_03_prize_at_anchor_i: You take the sloop under your flag and paint “Seafoam” across the stern.
You sell the sloop to a yard before an old owner comes to claim it.
You leave the dockworkers and claimants to settle a prize you do not control, or choose not to keep.
The dockworkers turn to you one last time. If you control the papers or the deck, you can still take the sloop or sell it; otherwise, all that remains is to leave the quay.
event.career_pirate_03_prize_at_anchor.c: You pay the vanished captain’s creditor and turn the prize into a dubious transaction.
You sell the information to another pirate and keep the freedom to wait for a better ship.
You slip under the first blade and end up in the water before reaching the helm.
You turn their own mooring lines against them; the quay cheers the capture before you cast off.
You board, but the guards drive you off before you can hold the deck.
You seize the helm and both guards abandon the ship.
event.career_pirate_03_prize_at_anchor.t: A smuggler sloop sits at anchor without a captain: its crew scattered after an arrest. Two men still guard the gangplank, and the whole quay knows the vessel has no master.
event.career_pirate_03_salt_chart_i01.ch: You replace the warning with your sign and turn a shortcut into a challenge.
You leave the mark intact; the passage remains a shared secret, not a territory.
event.career_pirate_03_salt_chart_i01.te: In the cove, an old marker bears a fresh cut. Someone else still uses this route and left a warning: “Once, not twice.”
event.career_pirate_03_salt_chart.choice: You memorize the channel without exposing your family’s original.
You follow the chart to an abandoned supply cache still known to a few smugglers.
You sell the location to a runner and keep the chart out of his hands.
event.career_pirate_03_salt_chart.text: Your family’s old chart shows a cove missing from every harbor map. At low tide, a salt mark appears exactly where the ink indicates a passage.
event.career_pirate_03_salt_chart.title: The Salt Mark
event.career_pirate_03_small_flag_big_se: You memorize one bearing before the cloth disappears completely.
You leave without a map, but with a clearer idea of what command means.
The old captain folds the cloth before you can copy the routes. “Good. Now find them yourself. A captain who depends on my line is still my passenger.”
You refuse to define your career by one kind of prize.
You choose routes where gold attracts hunters and Marines as well.
You prefer routes offering no guarantee except a story nobody has told yet.
An old captain traces two routes on a stained tablecloth: one promises easy cargo, the other islands almost nobody visits. He is not selling a map; he is asking what you chase.
event.career_pirate_04_double_crossed_bu: You leave the cashbox and make his betrayal an example worth more than the coins.
You take the money and leave him with a business nobody will trust as safe.
The fence ends up on his knees between his two doors. He offers his whole cashbox if you forget his name; outside, the hunters retreat.
You put down more money than the hunters and turn his loyalty into a simple auction.
You watch the wrong door; hunters enter through the one you thought safe.
You see the trap, the false floor, and the third accomplice; the whole ambush becomes readable at once.
You understand the betrayal just early enough to flee, leaving some money behind.
You spot the signal between the fence and the hunters before they seal the room.
You abandon the deal before the doors close and spread word that he sells out his customers.
A fence invites you into his back room for a quick sale. Before counting the Berrys, you hear the rear door open and a second voice bargaining over your location.
event.career_pirate_04_navy_net_i01.choi: You memorize the details they use to identify you and change how you enter ports.
You fold the poster into your pocket as a measure of how far you have come.
event.career_pirate_04_navy_net_i01.text: After escaping the net, you find a fresh poster pasted up before the chase is even over. The Marines corrected your description and raised the amount.
event.career_pirate_04_navy_net.choice.b: You pay a watchman who opens a service gate before the order reaches him.
event.career_pirate_04_navy_net.choice.s: You choose the one alley already watched; a baton stops you cold.
You make the patrols run into each other and leave while they block one another.
You avoid arrest, but the chase leaves you hurt and your face better known.
You change levels three times and leave the net before they seal the quay.
event.career_pirate_04_navy_net.choice.w: You force the officer to choose between arresting the whole quay or letting you reach the crowd.
event.career_pirate_04_navy_net.text: Two patrols seal the harbor exits while an officer unfolds your wanted poster on the quay. He is not searching for everyone: he gives your description to every squad.
event.career_pirate_04_navy_net.title: The Marine Net
event.career_pirate_04_port_under_siege_: You erase your flag: the townspeople owe you nothing, and you do not own their victory.
You say the mark means you will answer if someone comes for the well again.
After the raiders leave, someone paints your flag on the well door. An old woman asks whether the mark means protection, debt, or simply one lucky day.
You charge their barricade alone and end up beneath the planks they drop.
You break the barricade on the first impact; the raiders abandon even their supplies while fleeing.
You open a narrow gap, but the raiders keep the well until night.
You overturn the barricade and restore access to the well before sunset.
You pay what they demand, then distribute the sacks in front of them without accepting their authority.
You seize their supplies elsewhere and force them to choose between the well and escape.
When your flag appears, the townspeople do not open their doors to flee: they signal from the windows. A raider gang controls their well and demands food before sunset.
event.career_pirate_04_poster_on_wall_i0: You refuse to let one harbor choose your title before the sea does.
You accept the nickname for now; your next exploits will decide whether it becomes ridiculous.
That evening, someone calls you “Rookie” from a nearby table. The word gets a laugh, then returns a second time, as if the port is testing whether it will stick.
event.career_pirate_04_poster_on_wall.ch: You pay the innkeeper and leave with the first official price placed on your name.
You take the charcoal and correct the drawing yourself before the room.
You sign the wrong drawing and let the Marines hunt a version of you that does not exist.
event.career_pirate_04_poster_on_wall.te: In an inn, a child compares your face to a badly printed wanted poster. The drawing is wrong, the amount still low, but the whole room waits to see how you react.
event.career_pirate_05_black_market_lant: You ask him to sell one truth only: you want to meet the buyer in person.
You give him a false destination to resell to the highest bidder.
As you stand, the broker gives one last sentence for free: someone is also buying information about you, and paying better than you are.
You pay for the name of a shipowner whose next crossing promises a real score.
You pay for an uncertain bearing and a story impossible to verify before leaving.
You pay for the schedules and learn where the Marines think pirates travel.
Under a lantern painted black, a broker sells three pieces of information: patrol times, a wealthy shipowner’s cargo, and a rumor of an island absent from maps. You can buy only one.
event.career_pirate_05_captain_without_p: You keep final authority, but promise to hear every objection before deciding.
You let the deck block an order that would clearly doom the ship.
The storm moves away. A crewmate asks the question nobody wanted to voice: if the next order could cost the ship, who gets to say no?
You ask the deck for a solution before giving the new order.
You cancel your order in front of everyone and choose the hull over your pride.
You read the front badly; a wave hits the hull before the crew can shorten sail.
You cross the front at the exact moment it opens; the silence on deck becomes respect.
You hold course, but the ship pays for your stubbornness in torn timber.
You find a window through the storm and prove the course was risky, not blind.
After a failed chase, your crew refuses the course you just ordered: clouds close the horizon and the hull has already taken too much. Nobody leaves their post, but nobody moves.
The Captain Is Not Always Right
event.career_pirate_05_hunters_at_breakf: You take their bundle of targets and bury your portrait among the other names.
You hand back their poster and tell them to choose a bounty they can survive collecting.
The youngest hunter hesitates over your crumpled poster. He has realized the amount is high because several teams before his have failed.
Your chair catches the table; they pin you before the room can shift.
In two moves, their chains fasten their own wrists to the inn’s furniture.
You break their formation, but take a hit while reaching the exit.
You overturn the table, open the door, and split the three hunters.
You give them a lead on a richer pirate and turn their hunt into a transaction.
You pay for breakfast and ask them to wait outside if they truly want your price.
Three bounty hunters enter the inn while your breakfast is still steaming. The first locks the door, the second unfolds your poster, and the third tells the owner to step back.
event.career_pirate_05_island_tax_i01.ch: You break his chair before everyone and leave the office without installing a successor.
You keep a cut of the harbor without pretending to be king; the line between toll and protection remains yours.
event.career_pirate_05_island_tax_i01.te: The local strongman backs down, but his men still wait for an order. Several residents now look at you as though you could simply take his place.
event.career_pirate_05_island_tax.choice: You put down the money for the seized baskets and have every catch returned to its owner.
You pay once, memorize his men, and turn the humiliation into intelligence.
You sit in his place and announce that nobody pays while you occupy the chair.
event.career_pirate_05_island_tax.text: A local strongman has placed your wanted poster on his desk as proof that you must pay to dock. Behind him, his men seize baskets from fishers who cannot pay the same tax.
event.career_pirate_05_island_tax.title: The False King's Tax
You remember who pays whom; even without accepting it, you better understand the local map of power.
You refuse to become the next collector in a system you just challenged.
The kingpin has one chair removed. “Then stand, captain. But if you grow big enough, others will come asking you for the same thing.”
event.career_pirate_06_blue_kingpin.choi: You crush your own miniature flag and tell him no token will represent your crew.
You reveal what you want too quickly; he raises the price and makes you wait outside.
You make him remove the other flags from the table before speaking as equals.
You refuse his tribute, but leave without an ally and with his men watching you.
You turn his tribute into a one-off deal neither of you can call submission.
You pay access for this deal and make clear the coin buys no future obedience.
event.career_pirate_06_blue_kingpin.text: A local pirate kingpin invites you to his table and places four miniature flags around yours. “Here, everybody pays someone. If you won’t pay me, I want to know what you’ll cost me.”
event.career_pirate_06_captains_table_i0: You refuse the paper and leave them to decide whether they trust you without a guarantee.
You sign the shares but cross out the command clause: your flag does not change captains in a crisis.
Before leaving, the three captains want the shares signed. One also demands the right to command if the plan goes wrong.
event.career_pirate_06_captains_table.ch: You refuse to turn your flag into a fourth color on someone else’s plan.
You claim the first attack and the greatest risk, therefore the hardest share to dispute.
You choose the position that lets the others expose themselves before you reveal your hand.
event.career_pirate_06_captains_table.te: Three captains offer you a place around a map: a rich convoy passes in two days. Each offers a different share, and each clearly omits one detail about what they plan afterward.
event.career_pirate_06_paradise_whisper_: You memorize the names before letting the page finish burning.
You nail the page outside: those who pay to avoid you become part of your reputation.
The broker throws his ledger into the brazier before other clients enter. One page falls aside: several known captains are also paying to avoid your route.
You announce your real heading loudly enough that whoever waits knows you are coming anyway.
You feed the network a false destination and let it pay for your lie.
You follow false accounts and spend a day chasing a front man.
You trace the whole chain and also learn which harbor was meant to trap you.
You find a relay, but he burns his notes before you see the final name.
You connect the payments to a captain selling your movements to Marines and hunters.
In a Paradise port, a broker stops talking when he sees your flag. Then he turns his ledger around: your name is already there, beside three ports where someone pays to know your next heading.
You burn it on the quay: mistakes are for correcting the next course, not decorating the last one.
You mount the damaged plank in your cabin as a reminder, not a trophy.
The carpenter hands you the plank he removed. “Keep it. A captain forgets what orders cost once the deck is repainted.”
event.career_pirate_06_scarred_hull.choi: You pay the yard and accept that surviving sometimes costs more than a score.
You brace the wrong frame; the wood strains harder when the hull settles.
You find a cleaner repair than expected; even the carpenter stops grimacing at the hull.
You stabilize the hull, but several cracks remain ready to reopen.
You replace the critical pieces and give the ship a real safety margin.
You leave without a full repair, but decide the next exploit will not be worth the hull.
event.career_pirate_06_scarred_hull.text: The harbor carpenter drives his knife into a blackened plank and pulls out splinters. “One more sea like the last, and your flag will continue without this ship.”
event.career_pirate_07_crew_legend_i01.c: You correct two names and leave the rest to the harbor’s memory.
You do not interfere; the legend is already becoming something you no longer fully control.
event.career_pirate_07_crew_legend_i01.t: That evening, a nearby table improvises a chorus about your crew. The lyrics are wrong, but every repetition gives a little more room to the other names.
event.career_pirate_07_crew_legend.choic: You accept that your name carries the public pressure so the others keep more freedom.
You refuse to turn the story into a hero catalog and make the flag itself the shared name.
You mix up two exploits and embarrass someone in public; the laughter around the table dies.
You tell the crew as a collective legend; the children already argue over their favorite member.
You name everyone, but your speech sounds more like an inventory than recognition.
You tell each role clearly enough that the harbor remembers several names alongside yours.
event.career_pirate_07_crew_legend.text: In a port, children know your name but credit every exploit to “your crew.” At a nearby table, several crewmates laugh; one asks whether their names will ever count as much as yours.
event.career_pirate_07_crew_legend.title: The Crew's Name
event.career_pirate_07_government_convoy: You refuse the false trophy and go after the mail boat before it reaches the next harbor.
You let the shipment go but spread the method; the same trap will be worth less next time.
The last ship opens its chests in the confusion: ballast, not gold. The real shipment peeled away earlier disguised as a mail boat.
You shadow the convoy to its real weak point and leave the chests alone for now.
You see the cable a second too late; the hull takes the trap meant for your approach.
You trigger both safeguards against each other; the convoy discovers its own plan too late.
You force the trap to reveal itself, but lose timber and the advantage of surprise.
You make the trap fire on a decoy and open the way to the last ship.
You attack the slow lead ship and turn their bait into an open battle.
Three Government ships cross at dusk with no visible escort. The last carries sealed chests, but the first sails too slowly: someone is clearly expecting an attack.
event.career_pirate_07_name_reaches_ahea: You drink and let one quiet story join the others.
You pay for the drink; tomorrow her story will include one detail she did not buy.
A tavern keeper sets down a free drink. “Not flattery. It’s the price for being able to say tomorrow that you drank here without breaking everything.”
Your reassurance sounds like a threat; two more doors lock.
The baker brings his tables back out himself; the street stops treating your presence like an alarm.
A few merchants stay, but nobody trusts you enough to reopen.
You get the first doors open without denying what your flag represents.
You spend with those who stayed open and make their courage good business.
You ask for better prices and let the silence negotiate for you.
Before you enter the main street, three shops close and two taverns open their best bottles. The same name creates fear on one side and opportunity on the other.
event.career_pirate_07_old_home_message_: You fold the reply with your charts; it gives no heading, but closes an old one.
You read the line aloud and own before the crew where part of your story came from.
On the back of the letter, beneath a salt stain, your mother added three words: “Then keep going.” No order, no advice, no debt.
You write the victories, mistakes, and names left behind without turning the letter into a legend.
You send only a copy of your flag with one line: “This one is mine.”
You include Berrys and let the gesture speak instead of a long reply.
A courier hands you a salt-stained letter from your mother. She asks for neither money nor your return: only whether your flag became what you said you wanted, or another version of hers.
event.career_pirate_08_captain_at_crossr: You let him report exactly what you chose; let them build their calculations around one truth.
You switch tokens in front of him and leave him to decide which choice was genuine.
The same symbol is carved beneath every token. The informant smiles: all three offers came from the same network, which mostly wanted to learn what you would choose.
You take the treasure token: wealth and pursuit come in the same package.
You take the island token and choose a story with no guarantee of profit.
You take the village token: being feared can also keep worse people away.
An informant places three tokens before you: an escorted treasure, an island nobody describes the same way twice, and a village seeking someone dangerous enough to deter its predators.
event.career_pirate_08_new_world_gate_i0: You answer that your flag has never asked for a guarantee about next week.
You mostly memorize the current that made their blockade possible; the New World just taught its first lesson.
Their captain unhooks the empty fifth hook and throws it overboard. “Fine. Keep your rag. Here, you’ll have to earn it every week.”
event.career_pirate_08_new_world_gate.ch: The current pushes you into their supposed blind spot; their cannon is already waiting there.
You use their own anchor as a pivot and leave them spinning while you sail away.
You get through, but the hull takes enough damage for their laughter to follow you.
You read the current better than they do and cross before they can turn.
You refuse to treat their stolen flags as authority and seek another route.
You refuse a crew battle and propose the two captains settle the flag question alone.
event.career_pirate_08_new_world_gate.te: Barely arrived, an unknown crew drops anchor across your path and raises four flags taken from other captains. Their loudhailer announces that a fifth space is waiting for yours.
event.career_pirate_08_new_world_gate.ti: The New World Sizes You Up
event.career_pirate_08_stranded_legend_i: You let him sell the advertised presence of the famous pirate and take the reserved berth as payment.
You claim a share of advance tickets sold on your name; he pays without arguing long.
Before signing, the shipowner finally draws both flags at the same height on the contract. “My passengers pay better when they think they are traveling with a story.”
event.career_pirate_08_stranded_legend.c: You accept the berth under his flag without pretending your independence depends on a piece of cloth.
You pay for the berth like any passenger and keep your flag folded among your own belongings.
You let him sell your name around the future crossing, not command your flag.
event.career_pirate_08_stranded_legend.t: Your name opens harbor doors, but you no longer have a ship to moor. A shipowner reserves you a berth on his next crossing if you hang your flag beneath his when you sail.
event.career_pirate_09_crew_crown_i01.ch: You leave the paint untouched: their gesture remains distinct from the name you carry.
You add your mark beside theirs and make the title a collective memory.
event.career_pirate_09_crew_crown_i01.te: Even after putting the brushes away, several crewmates keep paint on their fingers. They were not only asking for a title: they wanted to mark that they were there to see it born.
event.career_pirate_09_crew_crown.choice: You have the word painted over: surviving a long time is not enough yet to define what you are.
You keep the title but consistently tell the names that made it possible.
You force the gesture too hard; at the next port, the title looks like an advertisement you wrote yourself.
The word leaves the ship and becomes obvious in taverns that already know your flag.
The word spreads, but without the enthusiasm it had on deck.
The title sticks because your crew tells it before you need to explain it.
event.career_pirate_09_crew_crown.text: After a victory, your crew paints a new word beneath your flag before you see it. “Veteran,” they say. Not a rank, not an order: their way of saying you have survived long enough to matter.
event.career_pirate_09_crew_crown.title: The Title the Deck Offers
event.career_pirate_09_legendary_heist_i: You copy the payments across several ports; the theft becomes a scandal impossible to put back in the chest.
You take the money and let the ledgers become somebody else’s problem.
Under the three seals, you find mostly secret payment ledgers and enough Berrys to fund several operations. The names are probably worth more than the coins.
event.career_pirate_09_legendary_heist.c: You deliberately spread the date and turn the chest into a public challenge to the Government.
You buy his silence and make him choose the hour when the ship will be most vulnerable.
You choose the decoy schedule; the escort is already waiting on both sides of the channel.
You realize all three schedules describe the same detour; you wait at the point they thought impossible to predict.
You find the right ship, but too late to avoid the full escort.
You strike during the one transfer when the chest changes decks without full protection.
event.career_pirate_09_legendary_heist.t: A Government pay ship keeps a chest under three seals and changes route nightly. A former courier gives you all three schedules: only one interception avoids fighting the entire escort.
event.career_pirate_09_world_sets_price_: You tell him the world can fill the line when it has something better than your name.
You accept a simple title: long enough at sea that the next one will not be given freely.
The seller points beneath your name. “People like titles. Rookie doesn’t work anymore. What do I print now?”
The Seller Asks for a Title
You buy the whole stack to see how your name changes from port to port.
You read what the world adds to your story without asking permission.
You write one sentence in the margin and let the seller decide whether he dares copy it.
A poster seller unrolls a fresh wanted notice. The number has grown, but the handwritten notes around it matter more: avoided ports, attributed jobs, contradictory rumors.
event.career_pirate_10_flag_beyond_you_i: You fold the flag without ceremony. Tomorrow it will rise because you still choose it.
You mend the cloth instead of replacing it; the legend keeps the marks of what built it.
When the young pirate leaves, you lower the flag yourself for the night. The cloth is patched and faded, yet everyone on the quay knows who it belongs to.
The Flag Comes Down for the Night
event.career_pirate_10_flag_beyond_you.c: You tell him feats matter less than what you are willing to sacrifice for each one.
You tell of scores, chases, and the times you chose risk in full view of everyone.
You tell him copying your life would be the surest way never to have his own.
event.career_pirate_10_flag_beyond_you.t: At sunset, a young pirate asks what feat someone must accomplish to “become like you.” Behind him, your own flag carries years of decisions impossible to reduce to one answer.
event.career_pirate_10_free_harbor_i01.c: You promise to answer once if their bluff is tested; after that, they must carry their own reputation.
You promise nothing, but leave stories of your choices as an example instead of your flag as a shield.
event.career_pirate_10_free_harbor_i01.t: Even after the decision, the residents admit the flag was only a shortcut. What they really want to know is whether your name will answer when someone tests their bluff.
event.career_pirate_10_free_harbor.choic: You let them keep the copy as long as they never claim to speak for you.
You turn use of your flag into a clear deal: their safety has a price, but not an endless chain.
You refuse to let your reputation govern an island where you do not live and return the mast to its people.
event.career_pirate_10_free_harbor.text: A small island flies a copy of your flag above its dock. The local council explains that no raider has landed since: they use your reputation as a threat without ever asking you.
event.career_pirate_10_free_harbor.title: The Harbor That Borrows Your Flag
event.career_pirate_10_storm_king_i01.ch: You let the papers use their word, but your flag still carries only your name.
You finally accept a title broad enough to hold the contradictory stories following you.
event.career_pirate_10_storm_king_i01.te: Before you change heading, a harbor skiff catches up. Aboard it, a seller already waves a proof sheet: the harbor supposedly “negotiated with a legend.” The word is printed beneath your name without asking you.
event.career_pirate_10_storm_king.choice: You refuse to let a governor choose your course with a purse, even a generous one.
You enter too fast; the chains tear timber and the harbor drives you back without firing.
You use the tide to lift their own chain; the harbor opens without making you fire a single shot.
You cross the first chain, but the hull pays for every meter and the governor does not yield.
You find the gap between two defenses and force the harbor to raise its chains before they can close around you.
You take the money without entering: the harbor just paid for the fear your name already produces.
event.career_pirate_10_storm_king.text: An entire harbor closes its chains before you arrive without firing a cannon. On the jetty, its governor holds your poster and offers a ransom simply for your flag to keep sailing.
event.career_pirate_10_storm_king.title: The Port Closes Before the Storm
