event.ch_combat_01_doorway_hold_i1.choic: The crate wedges under the handle. {{npc_childhood_younger}} shouts that the rear way is clear.
You push the wood, not the people outside. The latch holds a few more seconds.
You leave the door before it gives way and join {{npc_childhood_younger}} by the exit.
event.ch_combat_01_doorway_hold_i1.text: The latch starts pulling out of the wood. {{npc_childhood_younger}} has almost moved the last child through the back.
event.ch_combat_01_doorway_hold_i1.title: The Latch Slips
event.ch_combat_01_doorway_hold_i2.choic: You check the door while {{npc_childhood_younger}} counts the children outside. Nobody is missing.
You point to the exit the younger children used. The insults suddenly sound much hollower.
You give them the street. {{npc_childhood_younger}} waits until they turn the corner before exhaling.
event.ch_combat_01_doorway_hold_i2.text: The last child is outside. {{npc_childhood_younger}} stays beside you while the older teens realize there is nobody left to trap here.
event.ch_combat_01_doorway_hold_i2.title: Everyone Is Out
event.ch_combat_01_doorway_hold.choice.b: You put your weight against the wood. {{npc_childhood_younger}} starts moving the two younger children out behind you.
event.ch_combat_01_doorway_hold.choice.c: Your shout carries through the walls. Outside, the blows against the door falter.
You clear the rear passage. {{npc_childhood_younger}} sends the first child toward the light.
event.ch_combat_01_doorway_hold.text: {{npc_childhood_younger}} and two younger children shelter in a workshop while a group of angry teens pushes at the door. The back exit is still open.
event.ch_combat_01_doorway_hold.title: {{npc_childhood_younger}} Behind the Door
You attack the bend. {{npc_childhood_rival}} answers without thinking and you come out side by side.
You keep your footing. {{npc_childhood_rival}} cannot shake you through the bend.
You copy her foot placement at the last moment. She notices at once.
The path narrows between two walls. {{npc_childhood_rival}} is already dropping her center of gravity to take it without losing speed.
You slow by a fraction. {{npc_childhood_rival}} notices, bumps your shoulder, and laughs.
You take the rocks. {{npc_childhood_rival}} follows instead of letting you risk them alone.
You almost touch the trunk together. {{npc_childhood_rival}} is already demanding a rematch.
The fig tree appears at the end of the path. {{npc_childhood_rival}} is half a stride away, close enough to win or fall with you.
event.ch_combat_01_hill_sprint_rival.cho: You point out the slick ground. {{npc_childhood_rival}} grumbles, then agrees to walk back.
Your foot rolls on a stone. {{npc_childhood_rival}} stops dead and comes back despite the race.
You find your rhythm and move ahead. {{npc_childhood_rival}} laughs out loud and accelerates.
{{npc_childhood_rival}} gains three lengths. She looks back just enough to check you are still there.
You hold her pace into the bend. {{npc_childhood_rival}} finally stops smiling.
You avoid the rocks on the shortcut. {{npc_childhood_rival}} catches you later, annoyed by the clever line.
event.ch_combat_01_hill_sprint_rival.tex: {{npc_childhood_rival}} stamps twice at the starting line. “To the old fig tree. No shortcuts.” She takes off before the sentence is finished.
event.ch_combat_01_market_escape_i1.choi: You spot a gap close to the ground. {{npc_childhood_friend}} slips through right behind you.
You drag one basket aside and open just enough room to get through.
You turn back into the main street, where everyone can hear your side.
event.ch_combat_01_market_escape_i1.text: A pile of baskets blocks the alley. Behind you, the vendors are gaining ground and {{npc_childhood_friend}} is already looking for another way through.
event.ch_combat_01_market_escape_i2.choi: You call the first vendor by name. He finally gets close enough to hear you.
You step between them. {{npc_childhood_friend}} stays behind you instead of running off alone.
You peel the hand away without knocking anyone down. {{npc_childhood_friend}} moves again at once.
event.ch_combat_01_market_escape_i2.text: Two steps from the exit, a hand catches {{npc_childhood_friend}} by the sleeve. He turns instead of yanking away and tearing it.
A hand catches your sleeve and throws you into a crate. {{npc_childhood_friend}} comes back instead of escaping alone.
You read the crowd one second ahead. {{npc_childhood_friend}} follows without asking why.
The crowd closes the gap. {{npc_childhood_friend}} stays shoulder to shoulder so you are not split up.
You find the same rhythm and slip between two stalls before the gap closes.
You open a gap for him. {{npc_childhood_friend}} hesitates, then runs and waits farther ahead.
You shout loudly enough for the first merchant to hear. His expression changes.
event.ch_combat_01_market_escape.text: {{npc_childhood_friend}} crashes into a stall while running and the merchant shouts “thief.” Two vendors are already blocking the market exit before he can explain.
event.ch_combat_01_market_escape.title: {{npc_childhood_friend}} Mistaken for a Thief
event.ch_combat_01_rival_line_seed_i1.ch: You give one step to understand the next. {{npc_childhood_rival}} immediately tries to surprise you.
You reverse her grip and {{npc_childhood_rival}} hits the ground first. She bursts out laughing.
You shift her footing by half a step. Her grin disappears at once.
Neither of you finds the angle. {{npc_childhood_rival}} laughs through clenched teeth.
{{npc_childhood_rival}} takes you down cleanly. The dust knocks the breath out of you for a second.
You let her advance before pivoting. {{npc_childhood_rival}} nearly laughs at the worst possible moment.
event.ch_combat_01_rival_line_seed_i1.te: {{npc_childhood_rival}} hooks your shoulder and tests your balance. Her feet move fast, but she gives you one second to answer.
event.ch_combat_01_rival_line_seed_i2.ch: {{npc_childhood_rival}} grips your hand. “Of course there’ll be a next time.”
You replay each move with your hands instead of your fists.
You leave without a verdict. {{npc_childhood_rival}} throws a handful of dust at your back.
event.ch_combat_01_rival_line_seed_i2.te: You both finish covered in dust. {{npc_childhood_rival}} offers her hand without asking who won.
event.ch_combat_01_rival_line_seed.choic: You wait for her first move. {{npc_childhood_rival}} immediately realizes you will not rush in.
You step in directly. {{npc_childhood_rival}} plants her feet and waits with a grin.
You set the rule. {{npc_childhood_rival}} raises an eyebrow, then offers her hand to seal it.
event.ch_combat_01_rival_line_seed.text: {{npc_childhood_rival}} draws a line in the dust with her heel. “One round. No excuses.” The other children are already stepping back to watch.
event.ch_combat_01_rival_line_seed.title: {{npc_childhood_rival}}'s Line
event.ch_combat_01_rival_thread_s01_firs: You move the line again. {{npc_childhood_rival}} stares at you, then agrees without arguing.
{{npc_childhood_rival}} takes her stance before you finish answering.
Three months later, {{npc_childhood_rival}} is waiting in the same place. She has moved the line two steps and refuses to explain why.
event.ch_combat_01_rival_thread_s02_comp: You smile without answering. {{npc_childhood_rival}} narrows her eyes; she will find it herself.
You show her one mistake too. {{npc_childhood_rival}} repeats the move until she fixes it.
You split up with the same thought in mind: come back better.
{{npc_childhood_rival}} sits in the dust and points at your footprint. “There. That’s where I got you.” She waits for your answer.
event.ch_combat_01_rival_thread_s03_choo: {{npc_childhood_rival}} punches her palm. “Then we stop going easy on each other.”
{{npc_childhood_rival}} nods. “Then we count mistakes, not wins.”
{{npc_childhood_rival}} thinks for a second. “Then someone has to play the person we’re protecting.”
{{npc_childhood_rival}} arrives with a question instead of a challenge. “Are we training to win, to improve, or to protect someone?”
event.ch_combat_01_younger_in_the_ring_i: You do not step back. {{npc_childhood_younger}} uses the hesitation to move closer to the exit.
You shift the crate just enough. {{npc_childhood_younger}} slips through the gap.
Hearing their own names breaks the pack mentality. Two of them step back.
One of the bigger children shoves a crate across the exit. {{npc_childhood_younger}} is trapped between the wall and the rest of you.
You join {{npc_childhood_younger}} and leave together before anyone changes their mind.
You do not give them the last provocation they were waiting for.
You stay long enough for the threats to turn into muttering.
The way out finally opens. {{npc_childhood_younger}} is outside, but the three others are still waiting to see what you do next.
event.ch_combat_01_younger_in_the_ring.c: Your shout carries into the street. The three older kids are already looking for somewhere to run.
You provoke them just enough to make them turn toward you. {{npc_childhood_younger}} takes one step back.
You stand beside {{npc_childhood_younger}}. The three others now have to decide whether they really want to continue.
event.ch_combat_01_younger_in_the_ring.t: Three bigger children surround {{npc_childhood_younger}} behind the crates. She clenches her fists, but she is really looking for a way out.
event.ch_family_social_01_doorstep_guest: You close it. Outside, the man makes no attempt to push the door.
Close the door and call an adult
You show him where he can stay without opening the door further. He sits against the wall.
Let him stay under the awning
You notice he is not looking inside, only at the roof above the doorway.
You think you see a reassuring smile. When the man steps forward, you back away at once.
He is genuinely shivering and keeps both hands visible, away from the handle.
The rain hides his face and you cannot tell whether he is telling the truth.
A soaked stranger knocks at your door. “Just until the storm passes.” No adult has come to see who is speaking yet.
event.ch_family_social_01_eviction_notic: A neighbor reads the notice with you and promises to stay until your parent returns.
You mix up a date and think there is less time. Panic arrives before your parent does.
A recent payment is missing from the notice. You circle the line before your parent comes home.
The formal wording does not help. Only one thing is clear: three days.
You find the amount, the date, and the owner’s name. At least nothing is hidden.
You tear the notice down. The holes in the door remain, and so does the problem.
A red notice is nailed to your door: three days to pay or get out. Your parent is not home yet, and the neighbors are starting to read it.
event.ch_family_social_01_family_badge.c: His answer sounds nothing like the one at home. You keep both versions in mind.
You turn the bag toward yourself. The man gets the message and moves on.
You repeat what you were taught. The man listens without saying whether he believes it.
event.ch_family_social_01_family_badge.t: A man at the market notices the badge sewn to your bag. “Do you even know what that means?” You only know the story repeated at home.
event.ch_family_social_01_family_reputat: You tell them your name. The laughter dies before you need to say anything else.
You leave them talking without giving them your face to remember.
They change the subject before giving the detail you wanted.
One of them recognizes you and goes quiet. The other realizes why too late.
A name and a place come up twice. You know what to ask about at home.
You finally understand what they actually blame your family for, and what they made up.
Two adults ahead of you say your family name and laugh about a story you have never heard. One insists he “knows what your people are like.”
What They Say About Your Family
You ask the loudest adult a question. Within seconds, everyone is talking about something else.
You answer without shaking, but your cousin keeps smiling.
Your answer makes the table laugh, this time at your cousin.
You answer simply. Your cousin looks for a second joke and cannot find one.
Your answer comes out too loud. The laughter stops, but now the whole table is watching you.
You put down your napkin and leave before dessert. Nobody can pretend you heard nothing.
At the long table, a wealthy cousin looks at your clothes and asks loudly, “Do you always eat like that at home?” Several adults laugh without looking at you.
event.ch_family_social_01_friend_at_gate: {{npc_childhood_friend}} mutters, “At your place, I’m scared I’ll ruin something.” At least now you know.
{{npc_childhood_friend}} steps in, slips on the rug, and knocks over a bowl. Every eye turns toward him.
{{npc_childhood_friend}} stays a few minutes, stiff in his chair, then invents an excuse to leave.
You make room away from the staring eyes. {{npc_childhood_friend}} eventually forgets about his shoes.
You turn the awkwardness into a joke. {{npc_childhood_friend}} walks in laughing and stops looking at the floor.
You grab your coat. {{npc_childhood_friend}} smiles before the door even closes.
{{npc_childhood_friend}} stops at your doorway. He looks at the set table, then at his dirty shoes, and cannot make himself step inside.
event.ch_family_social_01_household_ledg: You push the ledger back. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} does not smile, but he does not reopen it either.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} half-closes the ledger. “Then I’ll come when someone needs you.”
You point at the entries you do not know. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} pulls out a second, much older notebook.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} sets his old ledger on the table. Your household owes three favors to the neighborhood, and someone has come to claim the first.
event.ch_family_social_01_late_lantern_r: You leave the old evenings alone and keep this one for yourselves.
You name the nights you waited. Your parent listens all the way through.
This time, your parent comes home before dark. The lantern is out, dinner is warm, and they ask what you want to do with the evening.
event.ch_family_social_01_late_lantern.c: Your parent stops at the nearly cleared table, then hugs you without a word.
By morning, everything is put away. Your parent barely speaks over breakfast.
You nearly fall asleep sitting up. Your parent carries you to bed when they arrive.
event.ch_family_social_01_late_lantern.t: Your parent comes home after dark, shoulders soaked and eyes red with fatigue. The evening dishes are still waiting on the table.
event.ch_family_social_01_ledger_s1_firs: {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} crosses one line out of the ledger before you even leave.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} explains the work, then lets you decide with the facts in hand.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} closes the ledger. “All right. But the line stays.”
A year later, {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} knocks with the ledger under his arm. A neighbor must clear her cellar before the rain, and your household is next on the page.
event.ch_family_social_01_ledger_s2_term: {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} stacks the old notebooks on the table. “Then we go through all of it.”
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} marks your choice with one hard line. The next requests will come to you.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} strikes your name out. For the first time, the page looks light.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} returns with three old entries circled in ink. “Your choice: carry this debt, verify it, or leave the ledger entirely.”
event.ch_family_social_01_market_errand_: You return one item. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} ties up the rest of the parcel without comment.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} copies the old price on the back. “Show them this at home.”
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} puts everything aside. “I won’t sell it before you get back.”
Under the new tag, {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} finds the old price. “Your list isn’t wrong. But I still have to count what leaves the shop.”
You stumble over the explanation. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} frowns and takes the list back.
You point out the date on the list. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} immediately sees where the mismatch came from.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} does not follow all of it, but he flips the price tag over to check.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} checks the tag: the price changed since yesterday.
You leave with the list untouched. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} keeps the goods aside for when you return.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} removes one item from the basket and hands the list back.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} rereads the list from your parent. The written price is two Berrys too low, and there is nothing else in your pocket.
event.ch_family_social_01_parent_weak_da: Your parent nods. This time, the refusal does not become an argument.
A few months later, your parent hands you another list, shorter this time. “I need a hand, not for you to carry everything.”
Together, you keep only two things for today. The rest can wait.
You walk past the list without taking it. Your parent gets back up alone a few minutes later.
You take the first line. Your parent crosses out the rest and finally exhales.
Your parent drops their bag and sits on the floor before even taking off their shoes. They hand you the list of things they cannot finish today.
event.ch_family_social_01_shared_bowl.ch: Pull the bowl back to you
Turn the spoon into a game
Push the bowl to the middle
event.ch_family_social_01_shared_bowl.te: Only three bites remain at the bottom of the bowl. The adult feeding you looks at the other plates before lowering the spoon again.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} agrees: one hour of tidying for one hour at the bench.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} puts the pieces away. “The offer stands if you change your mind.”
You find a solution {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} did not show you. He resets the exercise to check it.
You force a piece into the wrong place. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} stops it before it snaps.
You get stuck. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} waits one more moment before putting the pieces away.
You find the right order. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} slides a real tool toward you, handle first.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} sets three pieces of wood on his bench. “If you want to learn here, show me how you would think this through first.”
event.ch_family_social_01_two_promises.c: The first smiles. The other swallows their disappointment and says tomorrow will be their turn.
The second takes your hand. The first stays on the doorstep, annoyed despite the smile.
They find you under the table a few minutes later. Both promises have now become an argument.
They look at each other, sigh, then change their plans. You will not have to choose after all.
event.ch_family_social_01_two_promises.t: Both your parents arrive at once: one promised you the docks, the other the neighborhood fair. Each was certain today belonged to them.
event.ch_generic_early_01_after_the_fall: Someone else helps {{npc_childhood_friend}}. When he leaves, he looks at the bench before looking toward you.
Your shout turns a head. An adult arrives while {{npc_childhood_friend}} is still looking for you.
You stay within reach without touching him. {{npc_childhood_friend}} gets up by himself and sits against you.
{{npc_childhood_friend}} grips your sleeve until his breathing returns.
{{npc_childhood_friend}} trips beside you and hits the ground hard. He sits there with his mouth open, not crying, as if he forgot how to breathe.
event.ch_generic_early_01_barking_dog.ch: The owner pulls the dog back. {{npc_childhood_younger}} whispers a barely audible thank you.
You bolt. {{npc_childhood_younger}} is left behind, as angry as she is frightened.
You move between {{npc_childhood_younger}} and the dog. She does not let go of your arm until the next corner.
You back away together. {{npc_childhood_younger}} immediately claims she preferred this street anyway.
event.ch_generic_early_01_barking_dog.te: The tanner's dog lunges against its rope, barking. {{npc_childhood_younger}} freezes in the lane, too close to move forward and too proud to step back.
event.ch_generic_early_01_borrowed_broom: You catch everything. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} stays silent long enough for {{npc_childhood_rival}} to stop smiling.
Two lids hit the floor, but the jar stays on the counter.
You catch the jar and one lid before they hit the floor.
You slip in the flour and land in front of {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}}. {{npc_childhood_rival}} chokes back a laugh.
You put the broom down. {{npc_childhood_rival}} copies you, far too innocent to be convincing.
You stop the jar with your fingertips. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} looks at the broom, then at {{npc_childhood_rival}}, then at you.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} appears through the cloud just as a jar rolls toward the edge of the counter. {{npc_childhood_rival}} looks at you. “Run?”
You point at the jars. {{npc_childhood_rival}} puts the broom down just before {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} turns around.
You grab the other broom. {{npc_childhood_rival}} salutes you like a duelist in the middle of the white cloud.
You step back. {{npc_childhood_rival}} realizes too late that the third jar is still moving.
{{npc_childhood_rival}} grabs {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}}’s broom like a sword. Her first swing kicks up a cloud of flour and sends three jars wobbling behind her.
event.ch_generic_early_01_crab_in_basket: The crab abandons the boot for your finger. Your yell wakes the entire room at once.
You push the basket to its claws. The crab drops the lace and backs inside as if nothing happened.
Push the basket back in front of it
The sleeper wakes, looks at the living shoelace, then at you. Their laughter makes the crab let go.
You follow it without moving. It vanishes under a crate with four inches of shoelace between its claws.
A tiny crab crawls out of a basket on the floor and grabs a bootlace. The person wearing the boot is asleep in their chair and hasn't noticed.
event.ch_generic_early_01_crowded_corner: The vendor climbs onto his crate and calls {{npc_childhood_friend}} with a voice that carries across the market.
You get a little higher and spot {{npc_childhood_friend}}’s cap between two baskets.
{{npc_childhood_friend}} answers from the other side of a stall. He was looking for you too.
You call his name at the right moment. {{npc_childhood_friend}} raises a hand above the crowd.
Nobody answers. You stay put despite wanting to run.
Your voice cracks in the noise. {{npc_childhood_friend}} does not answer right away.
{{npc_childhood_friend}} lets go of your sleeve between the stalls. One second later, three adults pass between you and you can no longer see his head.
event.ch_generic_early_01_den_den_ring.c: A voice says, “Hello?” You answer with very serious nonsense. Someone on the other end bursts out laughing.
You slide it forward inch by inch. A hand finally appears through the doorway and takes the call.
Push the receiver to the door
The snail rings, and so do you. An adult finally enters, unsure which one of you to silence first.
The ringing becomes a muffled grumble. Once freed, the Den Den Mushi stares at you with deep offense.
event.ch_generic_early_01_den_den_ring.t: A Den Den Mushi forgotten on a crate suddenly opens its eyes and starts ringing. Behind the door, the adults are talking too loudly to hear it.
event.ch_generic_early_01_fallen_nest.ch: The adult understands when they see the feather. {{npc_childhood_younger}} keeps curious feet away until you return.
Show a feather to an adult
You back away to the wall. Two birds finally return above the nest, and {{npc_childhood_younger}} starts breathing again.
With leaves and a crate, you shield the nest from the footpath.
You push the curious children back. {{npc_childhood_younger}} stays crouched by the nest, relieved.
Draw a circle around the nest
event.ch_generic_early_01_fallen_nest.te: {{npc_childhood_younger}} crouches over a fallen nest, already reaching toward the chicks. Two children behind her want to touch them before their mother returns.
event.ch_generic_early_01_high_branch.ch: You climb back down before reaching the branch. {{npc_childhood_friend}} does not make fun of you.
You recover the kite without breaking a twig. {{npc_childhood_friend}} looks at you like it was a magic trick.
The branch snaps under your foot. {{npc_childhood_friend}} reaches you on the ground before even looking at his kite.
You free the kite and drop it straight into {{npc_childhood_friend}}’s hands.
You nudge the branch from the ground. The kite falls between you.
You wait while keeping an eye on the tree. {{npc_childhood_friend}} refuses to leave without his kite.
event.ch_generic_early_01_high_branch.te: {{npc_childhood_friend}}’s kite hangs from a branch above the path. He swears he can climb up himself, but his foot is already slipping on the bark.
event.ch_generic_early_01_red_mask.choic: The traveler comes back searching everywhere. Under the table, the red smile stays quietly with you.
Behind the smile, you find strings, repairs, and three older layers of paint.
You wave the mask like a flag. Someone calls the traveler back before they turn the corner.
The owner doubles back and finds the mask upside down on your face. They laugh before taking it back.
event.ch_generic_early_01_red_mask.text: A painted mask falls from a travel bag and rolls to your feet. Its huge red smile stares at you while its owner keeps walking without noticing.
event.ch_generic_early_01_red_mask.title: The Big Red Smile
event.ch_generic_early_01_rules_of_game_: You remember the missing detail: {{npc_childhood_rival}} called her move before playing it.
You mix up two plays. {{npc_childhood_rival}} clenches her jaw and looks away.
You spot the mistake: they were using the same rule to mean different things.
You are no longer sure of the order. Nobody can settle the argument.
You replay the move slowly. The accusation looks weaker than it sounded.
You stop it before the insults start. {{npc_childhood_rival}} picks up the ball in silence.
The other child points at {{npc_childhood_rival}}. “She has been cheating the whole time.” {{npc_childhood_rival}} looks at you, stung, before answering.
You jump in too fast. {{npc_childhood_rival}} and the other child only shout louder.
You propose one simple rule. {{npc_childhood_rival}} grins. “I’m keeping that one.”
Nobody gives in. {{npc_childhood_rival}} tosses you the ball. “So what do we do?”
You make each of them repeat it. The fight is over one word, not cheating.
You side with {{npc_childhood_rival}}. The other child cries foul, and she does not look away.
You leave the game. {{npc_childhood_rival}} takes the ball back without stopping you.
{{npc_childhood_rival}} traps the ball under her foot. “It counted.” Another child swears it did not, and the game stops around you.
event.ch_generic_early_01_small_delivery: You make the trip together. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} does not tease you; the parcel gets there.
You hand the parcel back. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} takes it without pushing.
You find the simplest route and return before {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} finishes tidying the counter.
You recognize the right door handle and deliver the parcel without getting lost.
You mix up left and right at the first corner and return to {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}}, annoyed with yourself.
You hesitate between two doors and finally ask for directions.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} gives you a small parcel for the house at the end of the street. You know the door, but this is the first time you are going without an adult.
event.ch_generic_early_01_storm_shutters: A gust slams the wood near your head. You freeze halfway across the room.
You hold the bottom of the shutter while the adult secures the latch.
The noise sends you back. The adult shouts for you to stay away from the window.
You wait for the gap between gusts and help pull the shutter closed.
You pile bowls, papers, and tools where the wind cannot catch them.
You stay away from the window and hold the door shut when the adult asks.
A shutter slams hard enough to knock down a frame. The adult beside you struggles with the window while loose objects roll across the floor.
event.ch_generic_early_01_tidepool_glint: You climb back to the dry rocks. {{npc_childhood_younger}} watches the glint until it disappears.
You reach into the water. {{npc_childhood_younger}} grabs your clothes when the next wave comes in.
The glint disappears under stirred-up sand. {{npc_childhood_younger}} swears it was still there.
The glint moves on its own: a tiny crab is carrying a scrap of metal on its shell.
You finally see it: a small copper medallion caught under a stone.
You stare too long and a wave splashes both of you in the face.
{{npc_childhood_younger}} points at a glint under the water between two rocks. Every wave covers it, and the water is already rising around your ankles.
event.ch_generic_late_01_chain_of_favors: You write the favor down. {{npc_childhood_friend}} rolls his eyes but lets you do it.
{{npc_childhood_friend}} holds out his fist. “Then we agree.”
{{npc_childhood_friend}} finally accepts, mostly so you will stop insisting.
{{npc_childhood_friend}} gathers his tools. “Fine. We’ll see when your turn comes.”
{{npc_childhood_friend}} helps you fix what you just broke, then refuses what you offer him. “Keep it. Help someone else when your turn comes.”
You run for someone who knows the signals. They understand the problem at a glance.
You read the current backward and shout too early. A sailor corrects you at once.
You read the drift before the pilots do. Your warning comes early enough for them to separate.
You see the danger but cannot tell which boat should give way.
You identify the boat being carried by the current and shout to its pilot.
Both pilots look up. One second of hesitation is enough to break their collision course.
Two small boats are heading for the same channel. The quay flag says “go,” but the current is pushing one straight toward the other.
event.ch_generic_late_01_shared_credit.c: You correct nothing. {{npc_childhood_friend}} picks up another board without looking at you.
You name each person. {{npc_childhood_friend}} straightens up, and {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} corrects his praise in front of everyone.
You point out the parts built together. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} understands before you finish the sentence.
event.ch_generic_late_01_shared_credit.t: {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} praises your work in front of the whole shop, without naming {{npc_childhood_friend}} or the two others who carried half the boards. They heard it too.
event.ch_generic_late_01_younger_lookout: You turn the idea into a challenge on the ground. {{npc_childhood_younger}} is the first to agree.
You pull her out of the plan. {{npc_childhood_younger}} complains in front of the others, then thanks you once you are alone.
You take the corner. {{npc_childhood_younger}} goes with the others but stays close enough to come back.
You leave. When you look back, {{npc_childhood_younger}} is still alone on the corner.
Three older teens want to climb the school roof and stick {{npc_childhood_younger}} on the corner as lookout. She says yes, but her voice shakes.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_coastal_01.c: The bottle stops moving entirely. In a way, you have beaten the tide.
After a few passes, you know exactly how far the water will rise.
Watch every return of the wave
This time, the bottle gets past the small wave and actually begins to leave.
Push it farther into the water
The next wave comes back empty. For the first time, the rhythm changes.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_coastal_01.t: The tide leaves an empty bottle on the edge of {{birthplaceName}}. Every small wave takes it, then brings it back to exactly the same place.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_entertainmen: The musician keeps playing and bows to you in the middle of the chorus.
Push the coins back toward the hat
Passersby slow down to watch you. Two new coins land in the hat.
The song ends. The musician counts the hat, shrugs once and starts playing again.
Close your hand around one coin
The coin spins until the end of the verse. The musician finishes just in time to catch it.
Spin a coin on the stone
In a square in {{birthplaceName}}, a musician spins and knocks over his coin-filled hat. The song continues while the berrys roll away.
The bottle quickly passes from hand to hand. Everyone invents a different origin for it.
Carry it to the first houses
A wave immediately brings it back to your feet. The second attempt works better.
Put it back in the water
The sea will not take it back today. Nobody else knows it is there yet.
Hide it above the tide line
The roll knocks against the glass three times, then jams in the neck.
A wax-sealed bottle washes ashore near {{birthplaceName}}. No ship is visible on the horizon, but something rolled up taps against the glass.
The column moves on. One recruit comes back alone a few seconds later, much less proud.
The drum rolls between two pairs of boots and a hand catches it without stopping the column.
Roll it back toward the recruits
The drum stops against your shoe. The recruit recovers it without breaking stride.
Stop the drum with your foot
You miss every other beat, but the last rank starts marching to your tempo.
In {{birthplaceName}}, a drill blocks the street. A small marching drum escapes a recruit and rolls toward the gutter, right in front of you.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_nature_01.ch: The bottle stops just before the gutter. Someone picks it up with very visible relief.
Stand up a bottle before it rolls
The smell makes you jerk backward. A voice from the shop says that was the correct reaction.
The piles match no recipe, but they are much easier to gather.
It is horribly bitter. You spit it out before the shopkeeper can tell you to.
Chew the end of a leaf
event.ch_opening_birthplace_nature_01.te: In {{birthplaceName}}, a basket of herbs and bottles tips over outside a shop. A sharp smell fills the street before anyone comes out.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_outlaw_01.ch: The paper is still sticky. Later, half the face is printed on your pocket.
Fold the piece into your pocket
Only an eye, a grin and part of the bounty remain. The number holds your attention most.
The man looks down the alley, then decides repasting the poster is less effort.
The face becomes almost whole again, but the bounty ends up across the forehead.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_outlaw_01.te: In {{birthplaceName}}, a man pastes a wanted poster to a wall. Before the glue dries, someone tears half of it away and vanishes.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_port_01.choi: You catch it at the edge of the quay with both hands. Behind you, someone claps exactly once.
Chase the one rolling toward the water
The docker recounts the crate, sighs and goes back to work. The fruit stays with you.
Your stack leans dangerously, but it keeps three pieces of fruit out of the water.
Stack the ones that stop near you
The fruit stops dead. A docker picks it up with one hand without letting go of his rope.
Stop a fruit with your foot
event.ch_opening_birthplace_port_01.text: On a quay in {{birthplaceName}}, a rope snaps and a crate breaks open. Citrus fruit rolls between boots while the dockers hold the rest of the cargo.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_royal_01.cho: By the time the procession comes looking for it, the ribbon has already become your treasure.
The guard takes it without breaking stride and gives you an almost invisible salute.
Offer it to the last guard
The ribbon remains behind the procession like a decoration nobody planned.
A guard turns, hesitates between scolding you and laughing, then comes to retrieve it.
Wave the ribbon like a flag
event.ch_opening_birthplace_royal_01.tex: A small procession crosses {{birthplaceName}} under the guards' eyes. A long ribbon comes loose from a staff and falls behind them without anyone stopping.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_rural_01.cho: The goat goes around you without slowing, but loses enough time to be caught.
Stand in the middle of the road
You do not catch it, but you learn exactly how far your legs can take you.
The goat pulls from the other side. The cloth comes back in two pieces, one for each of you.
Grab the end of the cloth
The goat hesitates, drops the cloth and takes the grass. The owner cannot believe it.
Offer it a handful of grass
event.ch_opening_birthplace_rural_01.tex: Near a road in {{birthplaceName}}, a goat escapes with a market cloth in its mouth. Its owner comes after it, much slower.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_snow_01.choi: The parcel almost disappears. The driver passes twice before finding it.
The tracks are easy to follow until the first crossroads, where they mix with all the others.
The driver finally sees you and comes back swearing at the turn, not at you.
Hold the parcel over your head
Something jingles inside. You learn nothing else, except that it is not bread.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_snow_01.text: On a cold street in {{birthplaceName}}, a delivery sled turns too fast. A small tied parcel slips into the snow without the driver noticing.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_urban_01.cho: You are not strong enough to right it, but strong enough to slow its fall.
You gather a small pile while the adults handle the cart.
The wheel reaches his boot. He traps it without letting go of the cart.
Roll the wheel back to the vendor
The vendor eventually fixes the cart, then discovers his spare wheel is occupied.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_urban_01.tex: On a street in {{birthplaceName}}, a vendor cart loses a small wheel. The cart tilts, customers step back and the vendor tries to hold everything at once.
The map mostly looks like three lines and a circle. You are still the only two who can read it.
Draw a map of the hiding place
You find a hiding place too small for an adult hand and just large enough for the coin.
The first vendor refuses the coin without touching it. {{npc_childhood_friend}} looks strangely relieved.
Suggest trading it for a snack
event.ch_opening_friend_cargo_01.text: {{npc_childhood_friend}} returns with a bent coin no merchant would accept. To him, it is perfect: the boat now needs somewhere to hide its treasure.
event.ch_opening_friend_cargo_01.title: The First Treasure
{{npc_childhood_friend}} inspects the pebble like treasure and immediately scratches a hold into the wood with his nail.
{{npc_childhood_friend}}'s smile disappears. He does not take the boat back, but he does not go very far either.
Hold the boat against your chest
The boat leans, spins and stays afloat. {{npc_childhood_friend}} crouches beside you to blow into its invisible sail.
{{npc_childhood_friend}} catches it, smiles, then immediately pushes it back. The game is decided without another word.
Push the boat back to him
event.ch_opening_friend_intro_01.text: A child your age stops you with a boat carved from scrap wood. “{{npc_childhood_friend}},” he says, tapping his chest, then pushes the toy toward you.
event.ch_opening_friend_intro_01.title: The Wooden Boat
event.ch_opening_friend_race_01.choice.b: You hold back enough water to launch both boats at once. The dam bursts behind them.
event.ch_opening_friend_race_01.choice.d: {{npc_childhood_friend}} immediately draws another. You decide that two crews have just been born.
Draw a symbol on your sail
event.ch_opening_friend_race_01.choice.f: Your boat jumps ahead, hits a leaf and capsizes just before the finish.
event.ch_opening_friend_race_01.text: After the rain, {{npc_childhood_friend}} arrives with two small boats. The gutter in {{birthplaceName}} runs to the corner: to him, it is already a sea route.
event.ch_opening_friend_race_01.title: The Gutter Race
event.ch_opening_friend_reclaim_01.choic: He hesitates for a long time, then accepts the trade. The boat stays yours; the resentment, a little less.
{{npc_childhood_friend}} pulls his hand back and immediately draws a starting line with his foot.
Offer a race for the boat
{{npc_childhood_friend}} lowers his hand and leaves. He looks back once at the end of the street.
{{npc_childhood_friend}} takes it without smiling, but still sits beside you to inspect the hull.
event.ch_opening_friend_reclaim_01.text: {{npc_childhood_friend}} waits outside your home. He looks at the boat you kept, then at you. This time, he simply holds out his hand.
event.ch_opening_friend_reclaim_01.title: The Boat Reclaimed
event.ch_opening_friend_return_01.choice: The sail holds better after three folds. {{npc_childhood_friend}} claims that was exactly his idea.
{{npc_childhood_friend}} chooses the fastest current and nearly loses the boat immediately.
Let him choose the first launch
You find a trickle long enough for three voyages. On the fourth, the paper starts dissolving.
event.ch_opening_friend_return_01.text: {{npc_childhood_friend}} returns with the same boat and a crooked paper sail. “This one's ours,” he announces before looking for water.
event.ch_opening_friend_return_01.title: One Sail for Two
event.ch_opening_household_bandit_01.cho: Three heads turn toward you. {{npc_player_parent_1}} covers your mouth, too late to stop the laughter.
Everything gets carried away except the sack you cling to. {{npc_player_parent_1}} comes back for it last.
You see figures leave the main road before the horses even appear.
Supplies roll across the floor at the worst possible moment. {{npc_player_parent_1}} has to choose between gathering them and leaving.
event.ch_opening_household_bandit_01.tex: {{npc_player_parent_1}} drops two dusty sacks by the door. Outside, a lookout whistles two notes and the whole camp suddenly starts moving.
event.ch_opening_household_civilian_mode: The rag arrives covered in dust, but in the right place.
Drag the rag to the counter
The shutter drops halfway. {{npc_player_parent_1}} has to open again, laughing.
You copy the motions without fixing anything. {{npc_player_parent_1}} lets you finish anyway.
{{npc_player_parent_1}} follows your finger and finds it immediately.
Point at the tool under the bench
{{npc_player_parent_1}} raises the workshop shutter before sunrise. The tools are in order, except for the one that is actually needed.
event.ch_opening_household_civilian_poor: The coin disappears into a pocket. {{npc_player_parent_1}} thanks you very seriously.
{{npc_player_parent_1}} counts again, looks at you, then gently lifts your fingers.
Cover a coin with your hand
{{npc_player_parent_1}} puts the coin back in the right pile and shows you the other two.
Push a coin toward the list
{{npc_player_parent_1}} reads the purchases aloud as if you could already choose.
{{npc_player_parent_1}} counts three coins before opening the shop. One is missing for everything written on the small list.
event.ch_opening_household_civilian_weal: The search begins immediately. {{npc_player_parent_1}} looks at you long before the steward does.
Slide the key under the rug
The steward freezes, then eventually lets you hear the whole keyring.
The steward bows as if you had returned a treasure.
Hand the key to the steward
It is the wrong lock. {{npc_player_parent_1}} takes the key before the second attempt.
Try the key on a drawer
{{npc_player_parent_1}} speaks with a steward carrying more keys than you can count. One slips from his belt onto the carpet.
event.ch_opening_household_marine_01.cho: Two recruits laugh while standing at attention. The sergeant does not, but {{npc_player_parent_1}} does.
Beat on it like a drum
The formation later breaks apart to search for the helmet. {{npc_player_parent_1}} figures out where it went before anyone else.
Push the helmet under the bench
{{npc_player_parent_1}} helps you lift it. The soldier gets his helmet back before the sergeant turns around.
Hold the helmet out to the soldier
An old corporal returns your salute with perfect seriousness. {{npc_player_parent_1}} immediately straightens your hand.
event.ch_opening_household_marine_01.tex: {{npc_player_parent_1}} carries you through the barracks yard. A training helmet falls from a bench as the recruits snap to attention.
event.ch_opening_household_orphan_01.cho: The basket scrapes over the stones. A baker sees you, hesitates, then closes the door without taking it back.
Drag the basket under the awning
A hand comes back out with a still-warm bowl. You learn that here, making noise can sometimes be enough.
You keep the piece until the older children stop watching your hands.
Clutch a crust to your chest
They take the best and leave you the bottom of the basket. What you remember is who takes what.
Let the older children choose first
event.ch_opening_household_orphan_01.tex: Behind a kitchen in {{birthplaceName}}, a basket of leftovers appears before dawn. Two older children are already watching the door, and nobody seems responsible for you.
event.ch_opening_household_pirate_01.cho: The purse vanishes between your feet. {{npc_player_parent_1}} finds it first and gives you a much less amused look.
Slide the purse under the table
A pirate tells you the face's name, then the number underneath. Everyone seems to know the second one better.
Point at the face on the poster
Three coins answer. {{npc_player_parent_1}} takes the purse back before its owner counts it a fourth time.
The tricorn drops over your nose. The table bursts out laughing and someone announces that the captain has arrived.
Pull the tricorn over your head
event.ch_opening_household_pirate_01.tex: {{npc_player_parent_1}} opens the door to three companions still covered in salt. A tricorn, a purse and a wanted poster land on the table before breakfast.
event.ch_opening_household_prisoner_01.c: The locks keep rattling, but you no longer have to look at them.
{{npc_player_parent_1}} says nothing, but stops taking their eyes off the hook.
The guard speeds up without looking. {{npc_player_parent_1}} pulls you closer.
Tap the bars when he passes
The guard passes, returns, then passes again. Very quickly, you know when the key will appear.
Follow the key with your eyes
event.ch_opening_household_prisoner_01.t: {{npc_player_parent_1}} keeps you close behind a barred door. A key swings from the guard's hook every time he passes the cell.
event.ch_opening_household_privileged_01: {{npc_player_parent_1}} moves your hand away. Even here, some doors do not open for you.
{{npc_player_parent_1}} takes you back without comment. The servant immediately steps away.
A servant catches the cloth before it falls and waits for {{npc_player_parent_1}} to decide whether he may breathe.
The guard bows before even understanding what you wanted.
{{npc_player_parent_1}} carries you through a corridor where servants and guards step aside without being asked. One gilded door remains closed.
event.ch_opening_household_revolutionary: {{npc_player_parent_1}} sees what you did and immediately places a plate over it.
Pull the cloth over the paper
Ink smears between your fingers. The visitor goes pale; {{npc_player_parent_1}} swallows a sigh.
Crumple the paper in your fist
The paper disappears into a sleeve just before the door opens.
Everyone falls silent one second earlier. In this house, one second can be enough.
A visitor whispers with {{npc_player_parent_1}}, then slips a paper under the tablecloth. Someone knocks before he can put his coat back on.
event.ch_opening_household_slave_01.choi: The piece stays with you until evening. {{npc_player_parent_1}} understands what you did without asking.
Hide a piece in your sleeve
Every head turns. {{npc_player_parent_1}} gathers the pieces before the overseer arrives.
{{npc_player_parent_1}} shares anyway, but keeps the smaller portion.
He always counts again before leaving the room. {{npc_player_parent_1}} waits for exactly that moment.
event.ch_opening_household_slave_01.text: An overseer counts the bowls before serving. {{npc_player_parent_1}} receives one, keeps you close and waits for the man to turn away.
event.ch_opening_rival_intro_01.choice.c: {{npc_childhood_rival}} stares at you, picks up three stones and accepts immediately. The race has become something else.
event.ch_opening_rival_intro_01.choice.r: {{npc_childhood_rival}} starts half a second before everyone else. She calls it “being ready”; you call it something else.
event.ch_opening_rival_intro_01.choice.s: {{npc_childhood_friend}} protests, then runs anyway. {{npc_childhood_rival}} points at you: “Next one is you.”
You spot an alley cutting the corner. {{npc_childhood_rival}} catches your look and smiles as if she just learned something about you.
Spot a shortcut before the start
event.ch_opening_rival_intro_01.text: A girl called {{npc_childhood_rival}} draws a line in the dust of {{birthplaceName}}. “Race to the barrel. No excuses.” {{npc_childhood_friend}} is already taking a starting position.
event.ch_opening_rival_intro_01.title: The Line in the Dust
event.ch_v2_birthplace_north_blue_01_swa: You give the entry cue too early; the boat has to pull back out and attempt the approach again.
event.ch_v2_birthplace_south_blue_01_can: The medical platform is reached. Before the transfer, the caregiver asks whether the splint hit a post or branch during the passage; his check will start there.
event.ch_v2_birthplace_south_blue_01_cen: Plot the mast’s route through the wide streets
event.ch_v2_birthplace_south_blue_01_kar: Call an emergency halt to the line
event.ch_v2_birthplace_south_blue_01_sor: Point out the spare boards for the trunk
A second courier bursts into the port crossroads: both recipients have changed handoff points, one higher on the inland road, the other on another pontoon.
event.ch_v2_birthplace_west_blue_01_auro: As the cradle is being aligned, a worker recounts the wedges: one is missing. The hull will not move until it is found, and the passage stays closed.
event.ch_v2_birthplace_west_blue_01_masa: At Masala Port, performers play at the quay edge while a small ship boards passengers. The crowd steps back with each act and closes the gangway access; you are given the boundary ribbon.
event.ch_v2_birthplace_west_blue_01_sank: The steps are clear. The pilot wants to leave without being caught by the same current again; he asks you to signal when the bow finally points toward the channel.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_after_the_fal: The adult understands what happened and takes over without making the child walk.
Describe the fall exactly
The adult takes longer to understand and the child feels forced to keep pretending to be fine.
Say it is nothing
The child finally accepts staying put while the adult comes closer.
Help them sit without carrying them
The child takes one step and their knee folds. An adult finally reaches the lane, but only sees a circle of children and does not yet understand the fall.
The Second Step
Your voice disappears in the shouting; the child thinks people are mocking them and tries to leave.
You calm the onlookers too; the child stays still without feeling humiliated.
The child listens for a second, then tries to prove they are fine by standing.
You give them something simple to answer and they stay seated.
Keep them seated by talking
You clear air and space, but the child is already trying to put one foot under them.
Push the onlookers back
You mistake the silence for courage; the child stands and staggers toward the steps.
You immediately spot the worrying signs and clear space around the child.
You see something is wrong, but too late to stop the first step.
You notice the unfocused stare and keep them from standing too quickly.
Watch their eyes and answers
A child falls hard from a low wall during play. They do not cry, barely answer, and already try to stand while the others crowd around.
After the Fall
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_boiling_pot.c: You let go immediately from the heat; some water splashes the floor and everyone makes you step back.
The tray supports the handle and frees the cord without spilling the water.
Slide a tray under the handle
The cloth pulls taut against the floor before it can drag the pot farther.
Step on the loose apron tail
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_boiling_pot.t: A pot of boiling water sits too close to the edge of a low table. An apron cord has caught its handle; the person wearing it is already walking toward the door.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_breakfall_les: The instructor repeats the move slowly and shows exactly where the arm must not lock.
You lock your arm at the wrong moment and the impact knocks the breath out of you in front of the group.
You turn the push into a clean roll and keep enough balance to demonstrate the finish.
You roll too late and end in the sand, unhurt but with the technique still wrong.
You spread the impact and get up without planting a hand into the ground.
You anticipate the wrong side and fall stiffly under two students’ laughter.
You spot the motion before contact and adjust your feet without breaking the drill.
You see the push but not its exact angle; the fall stays messy.
You read the angle and choose the right side to absorb the fall.
Read the shoulder before the push
An instructor drills falls on packed sand. After two demonstrations it is your turn: a partner will push you sideways, and locking an arm is exactly the mistake to avoid.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_cart_raid_i01: The stack tips the other way and leaves the driver safe.
Kick the bottom crate toward the wall
The thief gains ground, but nobody chases under falling boxes.
Let the sack go and secure the cart
The driver clears the line before the boxes fall.
Pull the driver behind the wheel
The first sack drops or vanishes behind stacked crates. A bandit shoves the stack to cover the escape; the top boxes start tipping toward the driver.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_cart_raid_i02: You gain a few meters then have to stop; the driver blames you for abandoning the cart.
The bandit backs away and runs. Some cargo is missing, but the blade leaves with him.
Give the bandit a clear exit
You recover what is within reach without turning the theft into a duel.
Keep distance and recover the dropped sack
Two bandits run. The last stays by the drawbar, winded, with a small blade drawn mostly to scare; behind you, the driver wants the sack back.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_cart_raid.cho: The wheel escapes you and the cart pivots, exposing its open side to the thieves.
You wedge the wheel against a post and turn the cart into stable cover.
You slow the cart, but a sack is already sliding off the bed.
You stop the wheel and keep the cart from becoming a danger itself.
You choose the wrong lane; the thief reaches the corner and a second sack vanishes.
You read the detour and reach the corner first; the sack stays behind without a fight.
You force a turn, but the thief keeps the sack and reaches the crates.
You close the lane and the thief has to drop the sack to get through.
The drawbar drops to the ground and makes it impossible to haul the whole cart away quickly.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_cart_raid.tex: Three petty bandits rush a stopped cart and yank its cover. The driver drops to one knee; a wheel starts rolling and one thief is already tearing away a sack.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_ditch_jump_i0: The stone pins the wood just enough to offer a foothold.
Pin the plank with a stone
The bundle lands in the dirt, but both hands are free for the crossing.
Throw the bundle across to free both hands
You point out exactly where to step; no one tests the soft bank blindly.
Point out the only solid foothold
A slab of earth slides into the water. One narrow foothold remains and the plank tilts on the other side; someone is still stranded across.
The last foot clears. The plank then drops into the water, unusable.
Nobody falls, but the group gives up the shortcut and loses time.
You save the plank, but the final crossing becomes clumsy and embarrassing.
Try to save the plank too
The last child is straddling the plank when a root cracks. One action will decide whether the group leaves together or abandons the crossing.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_ditch_jump.ch: Your foot slips at the edge; you drop into the mud and the bank crumbles behind you.
You clear the ditch cleanly and reveal a line that avoids the crumbling bank.
You reach the far side on your knees, but a whole clump slides into the ditch and shrinks the foothold.
You clear the ditch and immediately spot the takeoff point that still holds.
The plank pivots under your weight and drops sideways, taking stones into the water.
You find two solid supports and turn the plank into a proper little bridge.
Your bridge holds for a second, then sinks on one side; the crossing gets narrower.
You wedge the plank between two roots and make a precarious but usable crossing.
You knock loose clumps away with a stick and keep to the firmest crossing.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_ditch_jump.te: Rain has swollen a ditch across the path. One bank is already crumbling underfoot, and the detour would bring everyone back after the crossing closes.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_doorway_evacu: Each child crosses with one hand held before releasing the previous one.
Make a hand line to the yard
Yard light comes in and the first child agrees to crawl through.
Wedge the hatch fully open
A rough lane appears through the slippery floor.
Sweep the shavings with a lid
The hatch opens, but the first child freezes at the dark opening. Beyond it, a sack of shavings has spilled and made the floor slippery to the yard.
The Rear Hatch
Everyone exits through the route that was already made safe.
Finish through the hatch despite the shortcut
Nobody mistakes the opening for a safe exit.
Block the new gap with a basket
The last child hesitates between two instructions and comes out crying, unhurt but embarrassed.
Switch exits at the last moment
The last child reaches the hatch when a sharp crack comes from the main door. The beam shifts and the shelf suddenly opens a tempting gap toward the main exit.
The Beam Moves Again
Nobody runs under the beam while you work out an exit.
Seat the younger children along the wall
You clear the only exit that does not pass under the beam.
Dump the baskets away from the hatch
The hook holds the shelf at a distance and opens a narrow lane.
Catch the shelf with a long hook
In a neighborhood shed, a cracked beam knocks a shelf across the main door. Three younger children are still inside; a small rear hatch exists, but its route is cluttered.
The Closing Threshold
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_falling_crate: The stack collapses early, before the group enters its path.
Knock down the two bottom crates on purpose
The stack stops pressing against the wheel and falls in one predictable direction.
Pull the wheelbarrow away from the base
You focus on the wrong thing; the whole stack falls into the lane and the others drive you out of the area.
Try to save the top crate
A stack of empty crates leans after a wheelbarrow hits its base. The crates are light but tall; a small group is walking behind it without looking up.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_falling_frame: Light gets in and the person sees a clear way out.
Lift only the corner with no wood
The person gets out, but a post rolls loose and breaks a nearby decoration.
Rip the whole canvas away
The person follows your voice and gets out without crawling across broken posts.
Guide their hand toward the clear edge
The frame is down, but the canvas has folded over someone and hides the broken posts. They move underneath without knowing which way is clear.
Under the Canvas
The post slips from you and the frame falls sideways, trapping someone under the canvas.
You guide the fall all the way down and keep the post away from heads.
You slow the fall without stopping it; the frame collapses across the lane.
You turn the frame toward open space and avoid a direct hit.
Catch the side post
Your shouts mix with the crowd; one person moves the wrong way under the canvas.
The crowd opens a clean circle; the frame drops into empty space.
Most people step back, but someone remains hidden behind the stretched canvas.
You get everyone out of the line before the frame hits the ground.
Clear everyone from beneath it
The canvas loses its grip on the wind and the frame comes down less violently.
Tear the canvas along its seam
A large decorated canvas frame tilts after one foot snaps. Wind pushes it toward the street; several people pass underneath without seeing the descending post.
The Frame Above the Street
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_frayed_swing_: The rope holds once more, then snaps on the empty return. The others blame you for waiting for that sound.
The game stops before the rope carries one more load.
Stop the next launch by holding the board
Without a seat, nobody can restart the swing before checking the rope.
A makeshift swing creaks over hard ground. With each pass, more white fibers show at the upper knot; the next child is already sitting on the board.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_kitchen_greas: The tile pushes the cloth away from the threshold without bringing hands close.
Push it with a tile
You bypass the threshold and reach the other side of the room.
Use the small side window
The blanket pins the cloth and opens a low path.
Slide a wet blanket over it
The burning cloth falls from its hook near the threshold. The main exit stays open, but the fabric cuts the shortest path to the back room.
The Oily Cloth
The panel gives way and lets air through, but broken wood stays on the floor.
Break the light lower panel
The person finds the handle and finally opens the right way.
Call out where the handle is
You stay under the smoke and free the door from outside.
Crawl to the door and open it
A voice answers behind the back-room door: smoke hides the handle and the person is pushing the wrong way. Heat is building at the ceiling.
Someone in the Back Room
The mat keeps smoking and an adult has to run back. Your haste is obvious.
Say the fire is over
The mat ends up in the yard where the embers can be soaked without trapping smoke.
Roll the mat outside
Water cuts off the embers’ spread before reaching the center.
Wet the edges first
Everyone is outside when the smell of burning returns. Under a mat near the threshold, a few red embers are still creeping through the fibers.
Embers Under the Mat
The stool catches the cloth; the oily fabric falls burning to the floor.
You clear stool and basket in one move, leaving almost bare floor around the pan.
You pull the stool away, but the cloth still slides near the flame.
You clear the route and move the nearest fuel away.
Pull the stool clear
The salt smothers part of the oil on the floor, but a cloth is already blackening.
Dump the salt bin onto the spill
You use the wrong lid; it slips and a tongue of flame catches the nearby cloth.
You set the lid without moving the pan and push everyone back from the fire.
You cover most of the pan, but one edge stays open and the flame finds air.
You cut the pan off from air before the oil can spread.
Smother the pan under a lid
A pan of oil ignites in a shared kitchen. Flame is already licking a hanging cloth; two people are outside and someone is still in the small back room.
The Oil Catches Fire
The ladder forces you backward; it misses the window but you end on the floor covered in sawdust.
The shutter takes the first contact and the person behind moves away from the impact.
The wedge stops the slide before the top reaches the window.
Kick a wedge under the foot
A long ladder against a wall starts sliding when its foot hits sawdust. Nobody is on it, but its top is dropping toward an open window where someone works with their back turned.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_panicked_dog_: The gate forces the dog to turn before the collision.
Push a gate between them
The noise stops; the dog slows, but keeps moving toward the end.
Throw a cloth over the rattling baskets
The passers-by press to the wall and clear the alley.
Shout “left!” to the passers-by
The child is clear, but a shutter bangs and startles the dog again. It veers into an alley where two people approach without seeing it.
It Changes Target
The dog sniffs the bowl; the tension drops enough to wait.
Slide a bowl of water forward
Seeing an exit, the dog stops pressing into the wall.
Leave it one exit toward the yard
You pin the rope without entering biting range.
Pin the rope away from its mouth
The dog ends up under a stair, back to the wall, ears flat. Its rope is finally reachable, but it growls whenever a hand approaches.
Cornered Under the Stairs
The rope changes hands without anyone crawling under the stairs.
Slide the rope to her along the ground
She gets the dog back, but the sudden grab triggers one last bark and a sharp scare.
Let her grab the collar
She slows down and calls the dog instead of grabbing it. The rope finally returns to her hand.
Gently stop her hand
A neighbor runs up and recognizes the collar. She reaches too quickly; the dog tenses again, and everything you gained could vanish in a second.
The Recognized Collar
The baskets close the lane without trapping the animal; the dog slows enough for the situation to change.
Make a screen with two empty baskets
You slip in front of it; the dog bounds over you and its rope lashes your ankle.
You keep exactly the right distance and guide its run toward an open yard.
You divert the dog, but it immediately switches toward a more crowded stall.
You open an empty line and draw it away from the passers-by.
You think the rope is clear; it wraps a table leg and throws baskets into the lane.
You see where the rope will go taut and clear that space before impact.
You spot the rope too late to catch it; it keeps sweeping the lane.
You anticipate the rope’s next bounce and create a safe opening.
A panicked dog bolts from a yard with a long rope on its collar. It barrels through baskets; a small child freezes directly in its path.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_playfight_red: The others start shouting again and the pinned child mostly remembers that you chose the show.
Cheer for the fight to continue
You refuse to count the rest as play; the child on top finally gets up.
The familiar word interrupts the momentum and everyone recognizes the rule was crossed.
A playfight turns wrong when one child keeps going after the agreed signal. The other is no longer laughing and is pinned under a knee; nobody knows if the game is still on.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_runaway_handc: Someone misunderstands and crosses in front of the cart; every other option has to be abandoned to avoid them.
Your call opens a route toward an incline where the cart loses speed on its own.
The street clears late; the cart hurts no one but crushes goods on the ground.
People move aside and the cart ends its run in empty sacks.
Open the lane ahead of it
The crates break under the wheel and absorb enough speed to keep it away from people.
Drop two empty crates in front of the wheel
The handle yanks you off-line; the cart hits a stall before stopping.
You guide the wheel into the gutter and stop the cart in an empty angle.
You turn the cart, but it scrapes a wall and knocks over a stack of baskets.
You force the handle toward a post and the cart jams there without hitting anyone.
Grab the handle and turn it
A loaded handcart rolls alone down a sloping street after its chock breaks. Its handle whips side to side; farther down, pedestrians have not seen it yet.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_storeroom_int: The bell fills the street while you keep a door between yourself and the intruder.
Ring, then block the outside door
A board cracks under your foot. The figure turns and you lose the advantage of the doorway.
You work out where the intruder can flee and warn people without entering the storeroom.
After closing time, wood scrapes in a nearby storeroom. The door is ajar and a figure is searching sacks; beside you, a pull-cord bell rings directly into the street.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_storm_banner_: He crawls out of the danger zone while the bar keeps descending.
Send the merchant under the cart handle
The rope takes the load again for a few seconds.
Lift the rope back onto the pole
The cart turns and frees just enough room for the merchant.
Swing the cart by its handle
One rope slips its ring and lashes the pole. The bar drops on one side; a merchant is trapped behind his cart directly under the low end.
The Rope Whips
You use the cloth like a leash and lay the bar against the wall.
Guide the end with the cloth
The bar hits the stones without striking anyone. The festival lost a banner, not a passer-by.
Let it fall into the cleared space
You save part of the cloth, but the bar scrapes a stall and the merchant drives you away.
Hold the banner to save it
The last tie tears. One end of the bar drops toward the cleared ground while the other stays caught in the cloth like a lever.
The Bar Drops
You miss the cloth and the bar swings lower, directly over the lane.
You step on the trailing cloth at the right moment and the banner nearly stops billowing.
You pin one corner of cloth, but the other rope still whips and the bar keeps turning.
You pin enough cloth to reduce the wind load.
Run onto the trailing cloth
Two calls conflict and people cross paths under the bar.
Your call travels mouth to mouth and the whole lane clears before the next gust.
The crowd moves, but leaves one group trapped near the pole.
You open an empty corridor exactly under the bar’s path.
Clear the crowd in sections
The cloth loses one tension point; the bar stays suspended but spins more slowly.
Undo the lower cloth tie
A festival banner tears in a gust. Its long wooden bar still hangs by two ropes above a crowded lane; one attachment starts slipping.
The Banner Tears Its Bar Loose
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_storm_shutter: The bar comes free into your hands; the panel stays heavy but less dangerous.
Grab the bar before it falls
Nobody stays under the shutter, but the wood keeps pulling on the rope.
Clear the whole lane
The rope turns the fall into a controlled lowering.
Lower it under tension
The upper hinge tears free completely. The shutter now hangs from the lower hinge and the rope while its metal bar slides toward the edge.
The Hinge Tears Free
The bar stops against the stone and the lane becomes safe again.
Trap the bar against the gutter
You stop it, but the impact in your fingers leaves you shaking and embarrassed.
Grab it directly
People move aside and the bar ends its run against a wall.
Open a lane in front of it
The shutter finally reaches the ground, but the closing bar rolls downhill toward people’s ankles. The danger changed shape; it did not disappear.
The Bar in the Street
A gust tears you from the wall; the shutter swings again and nearly rips out its lower hinge.
You pin the shutter in the wind shadow and buy several clear seconds.
You slow the shutter without securing it; the screws keep pulling from the wood.
You hold the shutter long enough for a rope to be passed around it.
Pin the shutter to the wall
You turn the post into an anchor point; the tearing hinge still has to be dealt with.
Loop the rope around the post
You misread the rhythm; the next gust hits while everyone is moving in.
You spot a real lull and clear the passers-by before anyone touches the shutter.
The lull is shorter than expected; the hinge takes the load again before the rope is set.
You call the right lull and everyone acts during two calm seconds.
Wait for the gap between gusts
A squall hits the street. The upper hinge of a large shutter pulls from the wall; the panel slams above the lane and its closing bar starts coming loose.
The Shutter Becomes a Weight
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_too_many_to_f: All three turn toward you. You have to run and the vendor loses the time you meant to buy.
You keep the useful route in mind without giving the three adults another target.
Mark the courtyard and turn back
The warning goes around the street without your group entering the lane.
Pass a warning through a nearby window
Three adults with clubs search a small vendor’s bags and block the street. They have not noticed your group yet; behind them, a courtyard connects to another lane.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_tool_flash_i0: The bench breaks their line and keeps them apart.
Block the counterattack with the bench
The sharp command freezes the scene; the tool lowers without yet being dropped.
The trapped apprentice finally sees an exit that does not pass the other person.
The chisel hits wall or bench instead of a person. The impact shocks everyone; the armed hand stays tight, but the other apprentice now wants to lunge.
You separate actions from insults; the adult can act without guessing the rest.
Report only the actions you saw
The tension turns into anger at you; you leave the workshop under insults.
You protect the one who was cornered, but the other mostly remembers your accusation.
The chisel ends up on the floor. An adult runs in and immediately asks who started it while both apprentices talk at once and look for a witness.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_tool_flash.ch: The workbench creates a physical barrier without touching the tool.
Your words sound like a challenge; the tool strikes the wall to shut you up.
The room goes quiet; they lower the tool before anyone else moves.
The person hesitates but does not lower the tool yet.
Their gaze leaves the other apprentice and drops to the tool in their own hand.
Make them look at what they are threatening
You choose the wrong side; the tool flashes past you and hits the wall.
You read the move before it starts and pull the other apprentice out of reach.
You avoid the first swing, but the person keeps the tool between you.
You see the hand is shaking more than aiming and stay outside the line.
Read the grip before moving in
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_tool_flash.te: Two older apprentices argue in a workshop. One grabs a heavy chisel and raises it; the other is trapped between bench and wall, too close to step back.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_younger_first: On three, you push and pull together; {{npc_childhood_younger}} climbs with the rhythm.
Count the moves together
You haul them up quickly, but {{npc_childhood_younger}} immediately pulls away, upset at being given no part in it.
Haul them up anyway
{{npc_childhood_younger}} plants a foot exactly where you point and climbs one step.
Point to the crossbar
{{npc_childhood_younger}} finds one foothold, then pushes your free hand away. “Not like a sack. Tell me where the other foot goes.” The plank keeps creaking.

The question opens a practical discussion instead of an order to be careful.
Ask for their fallback plan
You refuse to act as final authority. {{npc_childhood_younger}} answers with their own argument, not a request for approval.

Approve the change

Ask what their version saved

Defend your original plan

The reply talks about signs, people, and limits, not what you would have done.
Ask how they decided
You measure their choice against your own again. The reply arrives polite but distant.
Explain what you would have done
For once, no advice follows. {{npc_childhood_younger}} understands the silence.
Simply write “good”
After the job, {{npc_childhood_younger}} writes that the plan changed three times and they had to contradict someone more experienced. “I thought of our old planks, then decided for myself.”
Their Own Judgment
You accept the reversal without joking. The relationship is no longer organized around who protects whom.
Answer as an equal
{{npc_childhood_younger}} answers warmly but does not yield: “Smaller, maybe. Not less capable.”
Say they will always be “the little one”
For the first time, you write with a real question whose answer you have not already chosen.
Send one of your own doubts
The last letter begins with a drawing of the old broken plank. {{npc_childhood_younger}} writes: “I do not ask you to save me anymore. If you ever hesitate before a risk, you can ask me too.”
Equal Before the Risk

Ask for one clear request again
Set down your object and ask for turns speaking
In a busy room, three adults speak almost at the same time. With your Mink ears, you hear every sentence, but the voices overlap until you no longer know which request was meant for you.
event.ch_v2_race_mink_01_listen_for_sign: The two calls overlap: one comes from the boat quay, the other from the crate hall. The adults already look at you as if your ears should decide alone.
You finally identify the call from the boat quay. Before everyone resumes, someone asks how to avoid relying entirely on your ears next time.
Near the quay, you are asked to listen for the call that announces a boat’s departure. Crates creak, gulls cry, and another very similar call sounds almost at the same moment.
event.ch_v2_race_mink_01_lt01_first_filt: Months later, you are again asked to “listen carefully.” This time, three people agree to specify who is speaking, to whom, and for what action before starting.
event.ch_v2_race_mink_01_lt08_layers.tex: A complex request arrives with three useful details and two noisy distractions. You now know to ask for the name, the action, and the deadline before sorting the rest.
event.ch_v2_race_mink_01_lt10a_familiar_: A familiar voice calls you from far away, but the quay noise distorts the words. You recognize the person, not yet the requested action.
event.ch_v2_race_mink_01_lt10b_source_be: A clear call crosses the street, but first you look for who made it and where they are looking. This time, clarity begins before your ears.
event.ch_v2_race_mink_01_trail_after_rai: Under the awning, tracks cross with drops falling from the roof. One fresh print leads toward the storage room, but a soap smell pulls toward the yard.
event.dead_end_at_sea.choice.follow_curr: You reach a destination where your story can continue.
event.dead_end_at_sea.text: The currents eventually reveal a safe continuation.
event.dead_end_at_sea.title: Land on the Horizon
event.dead_end_on_land.choice.resume_voy: You reach the nearest maritime access and cast off.
event.dead_end_on_land.text: No new lead presents itself here, but the sea remains open.
event.dead_end_on_land.title: The Open Sea Calls
event.family_civilian_01_fathers_work_be: You take the customer's coin and hold it out to your father. He laughs, takes it, and finishes the sale one-handed.
You tug his sleeve toward your bowl. Your father asks the customer to wait a minute and takes the spoon again.
Pull his sleeve toward the bowl
You push the coin toward the edge. Your father catches it and realizes you do not want to play shop now.
Your father opens the shutter with one hand and keeps hold of your bowl with the other. The customer sets a coin on the counter and asks to be served quickly.
You reach for him. He answers the customer without letting go of your bowl and slows down.
You clutch the spoon against your bowl. Your father sees the meal is not over before lifting the shutter.
You pat the counter. The customer leans toward you and your father has to serve without simply moving you aside.
Your father is still holding your spoon when the bell of his small shop rings. A customer waits behind the half-open shutter; the meal cools while he hesitates between you and the counter.
event.family_civilian_01_fishman_washbas: You put your hands back in the same basin. Your mother serves the customer with that water and refuses to replace it for his comfort.
You stay against her without touching the parcel. Your mother finishes the sale at her pace and keeps the customer at a distance.
You push the sealed parcel back toward the customer. Your mother catches it before it falls and tells him he can shop elsewhere.
The customer keeps his parcel closed and points at the basin as if it spoiled the whole order. Your mother looks at you before answering his demand.
